items.title: Routing
items.text:
Each node has its own speed test name, speedtest-<node>.<domain>. The node sends that name through the front door and the mesh to the homelab. A node answers the shared name speedtest.<domain> itself, and sends its requests on to the homelab as speedtest-<node>.<domain>.

On the homelab, your Traefik must send these names to the orchestrator on the port of speedtest.bind (8089). HomeGAP gives Traefik that route. You add no labels.

The route comes through the HTTP provider that you added to Traefik during the installation. See Install on the homelab. When speedtest.enabled is true, the provider has the route homegap-pages with these names:

  • speedtest.<domain>.
  • speedtest-<node>.<domain> for each node.

When you add or remove a node, HomeGAP changes the route. When you set speedtest.enabled to false, HomeGAP removes the names.

The route has no entry point, so it is on each entry point of your Traefik. It has TLS on, and your Traefik gives the certificate from its own TLS settings.

If a name gives a 404, see The speed test or the status page gives a 404.

items.title: The two tests
items.text: The Speed test page has two tests. Each test measures ping, jitter, download and upload.

items.title: Homelab to node
items.text:
The orchestrator runs curl on the node over SSH. curl connects to port 443 of the node, with the speed test name of the node. Thus the traffic takes the production path: the Traefik of the node, the mesh, the Traefik of the homelab and the speed test origin.

The test uses speedtest.streams parallel streams, and the rates are the sum. One stream shows what a single connection gets over the distance. Several streams show the capacity of the mesh link. In the results, "Up" is the direction from the homelab to the node. This is the direction of a download by a viewer.

The result also shows how busy the CPU of the node and of the homelab was in each phase, in percent of all cores. "kernel" is the part in the network stack and WireGuard. "steal" is the time that the host of the server gave to other machines. "busiest core" is the core with the most load.

  • If the CPU is near 100%, or the steal is high, that machine is the limit, not the network.
  • If the busiest core is near 100% and the total is low, one step uses one core only. More cores do not help.
  • If the two machines have free CPU, the limit is the network between them.

The test program on the node is a part of the load of the node.

To run the test, click Run test for a node, or click a node on the map. Test all nodes runs the test on each node in turn, and Stop ends the run after the current node.

During a test, a gauge shows it live: the round trip of each ping, then the download rate, then the upload rate. The speed test origin measures these as the traffic arrives. The final figures come from the node when the test ends.

items.title: Your device
items.text:
This test uses a short-lived link that you open on a device. The link is valid for speedtest.link_ttl. A person with the link can run tests until it expires.

  1. In the Your device panel, click Create test link.
  2. Click Copy, or scan the QR code with the device.
  3. Open the link on the device.

The panel has one link for the shared name, Auto (DNS), and one link for each node. speedtest.<domain> goes to the node that DNS selects for the device. That node answers the name itself and sends each request on to the homelab under its own name. The address bar keeps speedtest.<domain>. Thus the page shows the node, and each result belongs to a node. On HTTP, the node redirects to HTTPS on the same name.

On the page, Start test measures the path through the node of the device. Test all nodes tests each node in turn through its own name, speedtest-<node>.<domain>, from the same page.

The token is in the fragment of the URL. The browser never sends the fragment to a server, so no log contains the token.

A test link has these limits, so that a person with the link cannot use your bandwidth without end:

  • 8 streams at the same time for one link, and 32 streams for all links together.
  • speedtest.link_budget_gb (default 20) GiB of download and upload in total for one link. After that, the link sends and accepts no more data.
  • 20 saved results for one link.

The page uses 4 streams. A test between the homelab and a node has no such limit.

items.title: A VPN device with no link
items.text:
With speedtest.vpn_access: true, a VPN device opens https://speedtest.<domain>/ with no link from the dashboard. The front door must have a private path (homegap.private_network). See Client addresses and private-only services.

HomeGAP then makes speedtest.<domain> a private name of the front door. A VPN device resolves that name to the private network and gets the page from the homelab, not from a node. The page asks the homelab for a link, and the homelab gives one only to a request from the private network. A visitor who is not on the VPN still needs a link from the dashboard.

On this page, Start test measures the path through the VPN to the homelab. Test all nodes and the list of nodes measure the path through each node, on its public name.

The link of a VPN device has the same lifetime and the same limits as a link from the dashboard. Each VPN device that can use the private path of the front door can run tests. Enable this key only if you trust those devices with your bandwidth.

items.title: Results
items.text: HomeGAP keeps the last 300 results in <data_dir>/speedtests.json. The History panel shows them. The Path column is homelab ↔ node, device or VPN device. The node of a VPN device result is homelab if the test went through the VPN to the homelab.

items.title: API
items.text: Route What it does GET /api/speedtest Returns the settings and the recent results. POST /api/speedtest/nodes/{id} Runs a test between the homelab and a node. The call returns when the test ends. GET /api/speedtest/live Returns the test between the homelab and a node that runs now, or 204 when none runs. POST /api/speedtest/runs Starts a test of each node in turn. DELETE /api/speedtest/runs Stops that run after the current node. POST /api/speedtest/link Creates a test link for a device.

items.title: The speed test or the status page gives a 404
items.text:
Your Traefik does not have the route homegap-pages. Do these checks:

  1. Make sure that the static configuration of Traefik has the HTTP provider with the address http://orchestrator:8088/api/traefik/homelab.
  2. Make sure that dashboard.bind is 0.0.0.0:8088, so that Traefik can reach the orchestrator on their shared network.
  3. Open the Traefik dashboard and find the router homegap-pages@http. Its service must show the orchestrator as up.

  4. Read the address directly, with the dashboard token:

    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $HOMEGAP_DASHBOARD_TOKEN" http://orchestrator:8088/api/traefik/homelab

    The answer must have the router homegap-pages with the names of the speed test and the status page.

The service of the route uses the host name from the address of the provider and the port of speedtest.bind. Thus Traefik must reach the orchestrator by that host name on the two ports.

items.title: Status page
items.text: The status page is a public page that shows the state of your nodes. This page tells you what it shows, how it works and how to enable it.

items.title: What the page shows
items.text:
With status_page.enabled: true, anybody can open https://status.<domain>/. The page shows:

  • The node that the visitor came through. This is the node that DNS selects for the location of the visitor. The page also shows the round trip of the visitor to the homelab through this node.
  • The state of every node: Healthy, Warning or Not serving.
  • The round trip of the visitor through each other node that serves.
State Meaning Healthy The node works. In the data of the page, the state is online. Warning The mesh link of the node is up, but a check has a warning or fails. In the data, the state is degraded. Not serving The node is paused or in removal, or its mesh link to the homelab is down. A node also does not serve during a pause of all changes. In the data, the state is offline.

While the page is open, it refreshes every minute. Refresh loads the data immediately.

The page also has a map of the nodes in their status colors, with the round trip through each node. The map shows the homelab only as an area at the center of its region, for example "Home · North America". HomeGAP sends the location of the homelab only to a VPN device. See The page for a VPN device.

items.title: The connection of the visitor
items.text:
Below the node of the visitor, the page shows one of these lines:

  • Your address, with the public address that the request came from.
  • Connected to homelab VPN, for a VPN device. The page shows no address, because the request comes from the private network of the homelab.

The line Your address needs homegap.proxy_protocol: "true" on the front door. Without that label, the homelab sees an address of Docker for each visitor, and the page shows no line.

items.title: The page for a VPN device
items.text:
The line Connected to homelab VPN needs a private path on the front door (homegap.private_network). HomeGAP then makes status.<domain> a private name of the front door. A VPN device resolves that name to the private network and gets the page from the homelab, not from a node. See Client addresses and private-only services.

For such a device, the page is different in these ways:

  • The page shows Homelab in the place of a node. The round trip at the top is the round trip to the homelab through the VPN.
  • The map shows the homelab at the location that you set.
  • The round trip through each node does not change. The browser sends those requests to the public names of the nodes.

Without a private path on the front door, a VPN device gets the page as each other visitor does.

items.title: What the page tells a visitor
items.text:
The page and its data are public. For each node, a visitor can read these values:

  • The node id and the region.
  • The state.
  • The location that you set for the node: its name and its coordinates. The map uses them.
  • The name status-<node>.<domain>. The browser measures the round trip through each node on this name. The name resolves to the public address of the node.

The page does not show the IP addresses of the nodes or the management names. Each visitor sees only the address of that visitor. But a visitor can find the public address of each node from its status-<node> name. The public DNS records of your services give the same addresses.

items.title: Limits on requests
items.text:
The page needs no token, so HomeGAP limits its requests:

  • On the name status.<domain>, each node lets one address send 30 requests in a second, with a burst of 150.
  • The orchestrator lets one address send 1200 requests in a minute to the page, its data and the map. Above that number, it answers 429.

items.title: How the page works
items.text:
Each node answers status.<domain> itself, with its own certificate. This name never goes through passthrough. On HTTP, the node redirects to HTTPS on the same name.

On HTTPS, the node sends each request on to the homelab under its own name, status-<node>.<domain>. That name goes through the front door and the mesh to the homelab. The address bar keeps status.<domain>, and the orchestrator always knows which node the visitor came through. Thus the page, the node list and every ping come from the orchestrator.

For the round trip through each other node, the browser sends one request to status-<node>.<domain>. The request goes through that node and the mesh to the homelab. The browser measures the time with Resource Timing, from the request to the first byte. Thus the time does not include DNS and the setup of the connection.

When the homelab is down, a node shows its "back shortly" page for status.<domain>. See Failure modes.

items.title: Enable the status page
items.text:
The status page needs a front door. The status page and the speed test share one listener, which starts only with the orchestrator. If neither was on at the start, the first activation needs a restart of the orchestrator.

Key Default Rules status_page.enabled false status_page.hostname status A single lowercase label. It must be different from speedtest.hostname. status_page.title Status 60 characters or fewer.

items.title: Routing
items.text:
The status page uses the listener of the speed test, speedtest.bind. Your Traefik must send status-<node>.<domain> to the orchestrator on that port (8089). HomeGAP gives Traefik that route through the HTTP provider. You add no labels.

When status_page.enabled is true, the route homegap-pages has the name status-<node>.<domain> of each node. The shared name status.<domain> is not in the route. Each node answers it. With a private path on the front door, the route homegap-status-private gives the shared name to VPN devices only. It accepts only the source range of the private network. See Speed tests for how the route works and how to check it.

To put the homelab on the map, set its location on the Locations page. See Maps and locations.

items.title: Diagnostics and troubleshooting
items.text: This page tells you where to find logs and diagnostics, and what to check for common problems.

items.title: Where to look first
items.text:
Start with Needs attention on the Overview page. It lists what is wrong now, with the failures first. Select an item to open the page that has the details.

Item Meaning "The homelab can't reach any node" The config has two or more nodes, and none of them answers over SSH. Check the internet connection of the homelab. "<node> is failing" or "<node> has a warning" A check of the node fails or has a warning. The item names the first such check. See The node checks. "<node>: provisioning failed" The last provisioning run of the node failed. The item shows the error. "<node>: stack update failed" An update failed. With "rolled back; the rollout is held", the node runs its previous stack. See Node updates and rollback. "<node> has drifted from its config" A file or a container of the stack is different from the stack that HomeGAP wrote. HomeGAP repairs it, unless the node is paused. "<node> waits for its certificate" A new node serves its default certificate until the order with its management name completes. "<node> answers with the default certificate" The node does not have the certificate of the nodes. Open the Certificates tab. "The certificate order failed", "There is no certificate", "The certificate expires in N days" See Certificates. "<name> failing on <node>" or "<name> slow on <node>" The request to the service through that node fails, or takes more than 1 second. The item shows the status code and the time. "Label error on <container>" HomeGAP cannot use a label of the container. The item shows the reason. "<name>: <node> withdrawn" The health monitor of Bunny for that node is offline, so Bunny does not give the node as an answer. "<name> is not in sync" A DNS record is different from the record that HomeGAP wants.

items.title: The node checks
items.text:
The Inspector of a node shows its checks. See The dashboard for what each check reads.

Check When it fails ssh The orchestrator cannot connect. The check shows the error of SSH. See the SSH rows in Problems and checks. docker Docker does not answer on the node. traefik, homegap-maintenance, homegap-agent The container does not run, or Docker reports it as unhealthy. Read its log on the Diagnostics page. Then click Re-provision. tls-mgmt, tls-root The node serves no certificate for the name ("no certificate served"), or the certificate is past its end date. Open the Certificates tab of the DNS page. mesh The homelab and the node had no WireGuard handshake in the last 200 seconds ("no handshake with the homelab"). Make sure that the firewall of the provider has mesh.port/udp open (default 51821). Make sure that the homegap-mesh-agent container runs on the homelab.

items.title: The Diagnostics page
items.text:
The Diagnostics page shows the logs of the containers of a node. It also runs a read-only diagnostics bundle. Nothing on the node changes, and the output contains no secrets. You can download the logs and the bundle as text.

  1. Select the Node.
  2. Select the Container.
  3. Set Since to 15m, 1h, 6h or 24h.
  4. Click Show logs, or click Run diagnostics.
  5. Optional: click Download.

The page also shows the certificate that the node has and what the node serves for its names.

items.title: Log services
items.text: Service Container traefik Traefik. homegap-agent The agent of HomeGAP on the node. maintenance The maintenance page. crowdsec CrowdSec, with node_stack.crowdsec.

items.title: The diagnostics bundle
items.text:
The bundle has these sections:

  • The system: the kernel, the uptime, the memory and the free disk space.
  • The containers of the stack.
  • The mesh interface (hg-mesh) and the exit interface (hg-exit), without their private keys.
  • The addresses, the routes and the Docker networks.
  • The ports that listen, the firewall, and the NAT and forwarding rules.
  • The count of connection tracking entries and the last kernel messages.
  • The last 60 lines of the logs of Traefik and of the agent.

The Report panel gives one verdict for each section, for example "3 containers up" or "2 error lines of 60".

The API calls are GET /api/nodes/{id}/logs?service=&since=&tail= and GET /api/nodes/{id}/diagnostics. The default of since is 30m. The default of tail is 300 lines, and the maximum is 5000.

items.title: Logs on the homelab
items.text:
Use these commands in the HomeGAP folder:

docker compose logs -f orchestrator
docker compose logs -f homegap-mesh-agent
docker compose logs -f homegap-sign-in

With HOMEGAP_DEBUG=1, the orchestrator prints stack traces for fatal errors.

items.title: Other pages
items.text:
• The Activity page shows the reconcile log. You can filter it by domain (GET /api/log?domain=).
  • The Config page shows the differences between the desired state and the actual state (GET /api/diff).

items.title: Problems and checks
items.text: Problem What to check HomeGAP ignores a label. The label errors on the Services page, for example a hostname that two containers claim. The discovery warnings on the Activity page, for example "unknown label". See Labels. A node stays in a provisioning phase, or its provisioning fails. The Activity log and the ssh check. HomeGAP tries a failed first provisioning again after 5 minutes. SSH times out, or the server cuts it before login. A login blocker (fail2ban, sshguard or CrowdSec) can ban the orchestrator. Remove the ban from the console of the provider. Also compare ssh_allow_from with the public IP address of the orchestrator. A name does not resolve to the nearest node. The monitor state on the DNS page. Bunny removes a node that fails its health check. With one node, there is no other node to use. A site shows a "back shortly" page with status 503. The node cannot reach the homelab over the mesh. Check the mesh check of the node and the service on the homelab. See Failure modes. A service is failing on one node only. The mesh check of that node. Then the log of Traefik on that node. A browser shows a certificate warning, or a node serves the default certificate. The Certificates tab of the DNS page. Read the cause of the last order. See Certificates. The Pangolin app cannot sign in. sign_in.url in the config, and the log of homegap-sign-in. See Sign-in. With the Pangolin app on, only your private services open. The upstream DNS server in the app. It must be a server of vpn.tunnel_dns.resolvers. See Connect the Pangolin apps. A private name returns 403 on the VPN. See Client addresses and private-only services. Downloads over long paths are slow. See Performance. The log shows "the mesh agent has not reported". The homegap-mesh-agent container does not run, or it does not share the mesh data folder with the orchestrator. See Homelab stack. The speed test or the status page gives a 404. See Speed tests. The orchestrator stops at the start with a homegap: ... error. The config is not valid. An unknown key also stops the start. Run homegap validate. See Configuration.

items.title: Undo a first test
items.text:
To remove a test installation:

  1. Set reconcile.dry_run: true. This stops all further changes.
  2. In the Bunny console, remove the records whose comment starts with managed-by:homegap.
  3. Restore your previous records.
  4. On the homelab, stop the HomeGAP services: 
    docker compose down
  5. On each node, stop the stack: 
    cd /opt/homegap && sudo docker compose down

items.title: Upgrade the homelab
items.text: Use upgrade.sh to upgrade HomeGAP on the homelab. The script keeps access up during the upgrade. It also brings the files of the stack to the new version. This page tells you what the script does and how to use it.

items.title: Run the script
items.text:
The script is in the folder of the stack, next to compose.yml. Run it in that folder, instead of docker compose pull && docker compose up -d:

./upgrade.sh
Option What it does --no-pull Uses the images that are already on the host. --no-refresh Does not change the files of the stack. -h, --help Shows the help.

Each other argument goes to every docker compose call of the script. Such an argument also skips the refresh of the files.

items.title: Run it over SSH
items.text:
Over SSH, run the script in screen or tmux. If the connection drops, a script in a plain SSH session stops before it ends. In screen or tmux, the upgrade continues, and you can connect again to see the result.

The script checks how you run it:

How you run it What the script does On the homelab itself It runs. Over SSH, in screen or tmux It shows one line and runs. Over SSH, without screen or tmux It stops before it changes anything, and shows the command for screen and for tmux.

For example:

screen -S homegap-upgrade ./upgrade.sh

To run the script in a plain SSH session anyway, for example from an automation tool, set HG_ALLOW_SSH=1:

HG_ALLOW_SSH=1 ./upgrade.sh

items.title: Check the image signature
items.text:
The release build signs the homegap image with cosign. A signature shows that the build workflow of the HomeGAP repository made the image. The check is optional, and HomeGAP does not do it for you.

To check the image before an upgrade:

  1. Install cosign on the homelab.

  2. Run this command:

    cosign verify ghcr.io/drewcarlson/homegap:latest \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github\.com/DrewCarlson/HomeGAP/\.github/workflows/build\.yml@refs/tags/v'

If the image has a signature from a release build, the command shows the signature and exits with 0. If the command fails, do not run the upgrade.

items.title: What the script does
items.text:
1. It pulls the new images of the orchestrator, the mesh agent and the sign-in.
  2. It brings the files of the stack to the new version. See The files of the stack.
  3. It makes each data folder that is missing: orchestrator, mesh, identity, sign-in and vpn.
  4. It recreates the orchestrator. Traffic never goes through the orchestrator, so this does not stop access. The script waits up to 120 seconds for the orchestrator to start.
  5. It recreates the mesh agent (homegap-mesh-agent). The mesh interface stays up without the agent.
  6. It recreates the sign-in (homegap-sign-in). A connected device keeps its tunnel and connects to the sign-in again.
  7. It runs docker compose up -d --remove-orphans. This brings the remainder of the stack to the compose file. It also removes each container of a service that the compose file does not have.

If the compose files are not valid, the script stops before it restarts a container.

items.title: If the orchestrator does not start
items.text:
If the orchestrator does not start with its new image, the script shows the last 20 lines of its log. Then it restores the previous image of the orchestrator and stops. The mesh agent and the sign-in keep their containers.

The script restores the image with a tag: it gives the previous image the image name of the compose file. A later docker compose pull gets the new image again.

If the orchestrator does not start with its previous image either, the script stops. Read the log with docker compose logs orchestrator.

items.title: The files of the stack
items.text:
After the pull, the script runs homegap init --refresh from the new image. This command brings compose.yml, upgrade.sh and the example files to the new version. It never changes .env, compose.override.yml or the config folder.

The file in the folder What the script does It has no changes from you. The script writes the file of the new version. It has changes from you, and the script has a terminal. The script asks you. If you answer y, it saves your file as <name>.previous and writes the file of the new version. It has changes from you, and you answer n or there is no terminal. Your file stays. The file of the new version goes next to it as <name>.new.

If upgrade.sh itself gets a new version, the script starts the new version and continues from there.

Then the script checks the compose files. A new version of compose.yml can need a variable that your .env does not have. In that case, the script shows the message of docker compose and stops before it restarts a container. Set the variable in .env and run the script again.

To move your changes out of a file that HomeGAP changes, put them in compose.override.yml. See Homelab stack.

The script skips this step if the folder has no compose.yml, or if you give arguments for docker compose. If the refresh fails, the script shows a warning and continues with the files that are there.

items.title: The mesh container
items.text:
The mesh container (homegap-mesh) holds the network namespace of the mesh. It has a fixed image, so an upgrade does not give it a new one. The last step of the script recreates it only when its part of the compose files changes.

Caution

When the mesh container starts again, the mesh agent starts again with it. The mesh is down for a few seconds, and the nodes cannot reach the homelab during that time.

items.title: After the upgrade
items.text: The script does not update the stacks of the nodes. The orchestrator does that. The image of the agent of a node comes from agent.image, and its default tag is the version of the orchestrator. Thus a new version of the orchestrator starts a rolling update of the nodes. See Node updates and rollback.

items.title: HTTP API
items.text: The dashboard uses an HTTP API on the orchestrator. You can use the same API from scripts. This page lists every route.

items.title: Basics
items.text:
The base URL is http://<dashboard.bind>. Every /api/* route needs the header Authorization: Bearer <token>, with two exceptions. /api/terminal/ws uses a ticket. The Traefik of the homelab can read GET /api/traefik/homelab from the front door container without a token. The token comes from dashboard.auth_token_env or dashboard.auth_token_file. Without them, HomeGAP creates a token. See The dashboard.

With dashboard.sso, a request that the front door forwards for the name of the dashboard needs no token. The headers of the sign-in service give the user and the groups. A user in a read-only group can send only GET requests.

An action returns {"ok": true, "message": "..."}. If you can undo the action, the answer also has an undo id for POST /api/undo/{id}. An error returns {"ok": false, "message": "..."}, with one of these HTTP status codes:

Code When 400 The input is not valid. 403 A read-only user sent a request that is not a GET. 409 The request conflicts with the current state. 429 The address sent more than 20 wrong tokens in one minute. 500 Any other error. 503 /api/events already has 32 open streams.

Some answers have no JSON body:

Code When 401 The token is missing or wrong, and the request has no sign-in. 404 GET /api/setup/jobs/{id} does not know the job. 204 GET /api/speedtest/live, when no test runs.

Warning

The API has control of every node. Never expose it publicly. See Security model.

items.title: Routes outside /api
items.text:
These routes need no token:

Route What it does GET /healthz Returns ok. GET /map/... The tiles of the map (with range requests), its scripts, its fonts and its icons. The public listener also serves them when the status page is enabled. GET /docs/... These docs. GET /... Any other path returns the dashboard app.

items.title: Status and log
items.text: Route What it does GET /api/status Returns the full status snapshot. GET /api/events?after=SEQ Server-sent events. The first event is status, with the full snapshot. After that, a patch event sends the top-level fields of the snapshot that changed. The log event sends the new log entries after SEQ. The stream also sends metrics, job, speedtest and access events. GET /api/metrics?range=&edge= Returns the series of the graphs. range is in seconds. The default is one hour, and the maximum is one day. edge selects one node. GET /api/log?domain=&level=&q=&before=&limit= Returns the recent reconcile log. before=SEQ gives older entries. The default of limit is 300, and the maximum is 1000. GET /api/search?q= Searches the config keys, the names of the referenced secrets and the reconcile log. It never returns a value of the config. q needs two characters or more.

items.title: Config
items.text: Route What it does GET /api/config Returns the path and the text of the config file, the nodes and writable. GET /api/diff Returns the items of the diff between desired and actual state, and the effective desired state. GET /api/secrets Returns the referenced secrets: names, sources and presence. It never returns the values.

items.title: Control
items.text: Route What it does POST /api/resync Queues a pass. With ?apply=once, that pass applies the changes that wait, and the global pause stays on. POST /api/undo/{id} Undoes an action, with the undo id from its answer. POST /api/pause Pauses or resumes. Body: {"scope": "global", "id": null, "paused": true}. The scope is global, node or service.

items.title: Certificates
items.text:
The status snapshot has a certificates part. It holds the facts of the certificate: the names, the dates, the issuer, the serial number and the fingerprint. It also holds the state and the history of the orders, and the delivery to each node. The TLS probes and the state of the CAA records are there too. It never holds a key, a certificate file, the ACME account key or a challenge value.

Route What it does POST /api/certificates/order Starts the order of the certificate in the next pass. POST /api/certificates/replace-key Orders a new certificate with a new key, and revokes the old certificate. POST /api/certificates/check Runs the TLS probes of each public name through each node again. POST /api/certificates/nodes/{id}/resend Sends the certificate to the node again in the next pass.

items.title: Nodes
items.text: Route What it does POST /api/nodes Adds a node. The body is a JSON object with id, host and sshKeyFile. Optional fields are region, provider, os, sshUser, sshPort, latitude, longitude, locationName, managementHost and sshAllowFrom. HomeGAP writes the config file again, with a backup. DELETE /api/nodes/{id} Removes a node from the config. DNS drains first. The stack stays up until the decommission. The answer has an undo id. PUT /api/nodes/{id}/location Sets the location of a node. Body: {"location": {...}}, as for the homelab. HomeGAP writes the config file again. POST /api/nodes/{id}/provision Queues a full provisioning of the node. POST /api/nodes/{id}/update/retry Applies a held update to the node again. POST /api/nodes/{id}/update/skip Leaves the node on its current stack, and continues the rollout. POST /api/nodes/{id}/decommission?confirm={id} Removes the stack, the exit interface, the mesh interface and the contents of the install directory of a removed node. Then HomeGAP forgets the node. confirm must repeat the node id. If the teardown fails, the call returns an error and the node stays. With force=true, HomeGAP forgets the node without a teardown. GET /api/nodes/{id}/logs?service=&since=&tail= Returns the logs of a container. service is a container of the node stack. See Diagnostics and troubleshooting. The default of since is 30m. The default of tail is 300 lines, and the maximum is 5000. GET /api/nodes/{id}/diagnostics Returns the read-only diagnostics bundle of the node: {node, title, text, at}.

items.title: Terminal
items.text:
When dashboard.terminal is off, the routes that start a shell or give a ticket answer with an error. GET /api/terminal then returns enabled: false.

Route What it does GET /api/terminal Returns enabled and the open sessions. POST /api/nodes/{id}/terminal?rows=N&columns=N Starts a shell on the node and returns its session. POST /api/terminal/{id}/ticket Returns a ticket for one WebSocket connection to the session. The ticket works one time, for 30 seconds. DELETE /api/terminal/{id} Ends the session. GET /api/terminal/ws?ticket=TICKET The WebSocket of the session. It needs no bearer token, because a browser cannot send one. The ticket is the check, and the Origin header must be the host of the dashboard.

On the WebSocket, a binary frame has the bytes of the terminal: input from the browser, and output from the shell. A text frame has a JSON message with a type:

Type From Fields What it means hello Orchestrator offset The first message. offset is the position of the next output byte in the output of the session. exit Orchestrator code The shell ended. resize Browser rows, columns The new size of the terminal. ack Browser offset The browser has shown the output up to this position. The orchestrator stops the output while the browser is more than 128 KiB behind.

A new connection first gets the last output of the session, at most 256 KiB.

items.title: Node setup (the add-node wizard)
items.text: Route What it does POST /api/setup/test Tests an initial SSH login. Body: host, port, user, password or keyFile, resetHostKey and hostKeyFingerprint. A password login to a server with no recorded host key first returns the fingerprint. Send the test again with the fingerprint that you confirmed in hostKeyFingerprint. POST /api/setup/keys Generates, imports or describes the SSH key of a node. Body: nodeId, mode, and privateKey or path. POST /api/setup/jobs Starts a setup job. GET /api/setup/jobs/{id} Returns the progress of a setup job.

items.title: Zone records
items.text:
Route What it does GET /api/dns/zones Returns each DNS zone with every record in it. Each record has its kind: OWN, MANAGED or CHALLENGE. POST /api/dns/zones/{zone}/records Adds a record of your own to the zone. PUT /api/dns/zones/{zone}/records/{id} Changes a record of your own. The type of a record does not change. DELETE /api/dns/zones/{zone}/records/{id} Deletes a record of your own.

A change to a record that HomeGAP manages gets a 400, as does a record that collides with a managed record set.

items.title: Locations
items.text: Route What it does GET /api/locations Returns the known locations (shipped and local) and the location of the homelab. PUT /api/locations/{id} Adds or edits a location. DELETE /api/locations/{id}?reset= Removes a location. A shipped location becomes hidden. With reset=true, an edited shipped location goes back to the original. PUT /api/homelab/location Sets the location of the homelab. Body: {"location": {"latitude": ..., "longitude": ..., "name": "..."}}, or {"location": null} to clear it.

items.title: Access
items.text:
These routes serve the Access page. They name a role and a device by a number, which GET /api/access gives. See Users, machines and devices.

Route What it does GET /api/access Returns the roles, the users and the devices, and the address that the apps connect to. Without sign_in.url, it returns available: false and a note. POST /api/access/users Adds a user. Body: {"email": "...", "roleIds": [...], "password": "..."}. Without password, HomeGAP makes one, and the answer has it one time. DELETE /api/access/users/{id} Removes a user. HomeGAP refuses to remove the last admin. PUT /api/access/users/{id}/roles Sets the roles of a user. Body: {"roleIds": [...]}. POST /api/access/users/{id}/password Gives a user a new password. The answer has it one time. POST /api/access/users/{id}/{action} Does an action on a user: block or unblock. POST /api/access/machines Adds a machine. Body: {"name": "...", "roleIds": [...]}. The answer has the id and the secret of the machine one time. POST /api/access/devices/{id}/{action} Does an action on a device or a machine: block, unblock or delete.

items.title: Identity
items.text:
The commands homegap user and homegap machine use these routes. They name a role by its name and a user or a machine by its id.

Route What it does GET /api/identity/users Returns the users: id, email address, name, roles, blocked, hasPassword and createdAt. POST /api/identity/users Adds a user. Body: {"email": "...", "name": "...", "roles": [...]}. The answer has a new password one time. PUT /api/identity/users/{id}/roles Sets the roles of a user. Body: {"roles": [...]}. POST /api/identity/users/{id}/password Gives a user a new password. The answer has it one time. POST /api/identity/users/{id}/block Blocks a user. POST /api/identity/users/{id}/unblock Ends the block of a user. DELETE /api/identity/users/{id} Removes a user. GET /api/identity/machines Returns the machines: id, name, roles, blocked and createdAt. POST /api/identity/machines Adds a machine. Body: {"name": "...", "roles": [...]}. The answer has the secret one time. DELETE /api/identity/machines/{id} Removes a machine.

items.title: Speed test
items.text: Route What it does GET /api/speedtest Returns the settings and the recent results. POST /api/speedtest/nodes/{id}?streams=N Runs a test between the homelab and a node. The call returns when the test ends. streams is optional. GET /api/speedtest/live Returns the test between the homelab and a node that runs now. POST /api/speedtest/runs?streams=N Starts a test of every node, one node at a time. The status snapshot has the progress. DELETE /api/speedtest/runs Stops that run. POST /api/speedtest/link Creates a test link for a device.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
To read the status, set TOKEN to your dashboard token. Then run this command:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:8088/api/status

To queue a pass:

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:8088/api/resync

To follow the events (after=SEQ continues the log from an entry):

curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:8088/api/events

items.title: Command line
items.text:
The homegap binary has one command for each role. This page lists the commands, their options and their output.

In the container, run a command with docker compose exec orchestrator homegap <command>. The entrypoint of the image is tini -- homegap, and the default command is run.

items.title: run
items.text:
homegap [run] [--config PATH] [--dry-run] [--once]

Runs the orchestrator. This is the default command.

Option What it does --config PATH The config file. See Configuration. --dry-run Runs in dry run. HOMEGAP_DRY_RUN with 1, true or yes does the same. --once Runs one pass, without the dashboard and the public listener, then stops.

items.title: mesh
items.text:
homegap mesh [--dir PATH]

Runs the mesh agent of the homelab, in the homegap-mesh-agent container. It keeps the mesh interface, the interface of the VPN devices and the firewall of the namespace that it runs in. See Mesh.

Option Default Environment variable --dir PATH /mesh HOMEGAP_MESH_DIR

The agent reads the connected devices of the VPN from the folder /vpn. HOMEGAP_VPN_DIR sets a different folder. If the mesh folder is not a mount, the command prints a warning on stderr.

items.title: node-agent
items.text:
homegap node-agent [--dir PATH] [--state PATH]

Runs the agent of a node, on the node. HomeGAP starts it in the homegap-agent container of the node stack, so you do not run it yourself.

Option Default What it is --dir PATH /agent The folder with the instructions from the orchestrator. --state PATH /agent-state The folder that the agent writes, for example the key of its exit.

items.title: sign-in
items.text:
homegap sign-in [--config PATH] [--dir PATH] [--identity PATH] [--port N]

Runs the public sign-in of the homelab, in the homegap-sign-in container. It reads only the sign_in and vpn parts of the config. With no config file, it accepts passwords only. See Sign-in.

Option Default Environment variable --dir PATH /sign-in HOMEGAP_SIGN_IN_DIR --identity PATH /identity HOMEGAP_IDENTITY_DIR --port N 8090 None.

With sign_in.oidc, the command needs the client secret in the variable that sign_in.oidc.client_secret_env names. Without it, the command stops with an error.

items.title: validate
items.text:
homegap validate [--config PATH]

Checks the config file. If the file is valid, the command prints OK: <n> node(s), domain <domain>, zone <zone>. If not, it prints Invalid configuration: and the list of errors.

items.title: plan
items.text:
homegap plan [--config PATH] --labels FILE

Prints the desired state for a set of labels, without Docker. The file is a JSON map of container names to their labels. See Services.

The output has these lines, in this order:

ERROR <container>: ...
WARN  <container>: ...
node <id> (<management host>)
  public  ...
  private ...
  sni     ...
  port    ...
dns <type> <fqdn> -> <value> [<node>] <purpose> [geo] monitor=<monitor>

items.title: render-node
items.text:
homegap render-node ID [--config PATH]

Prints the stack files that HomeGAP writes to a node, with the secrets redacted. The last file is the dynamic routes file. The command reads only the config file, so the output has no services from labels.

items.title: user
items.text:
homegap user list
homegap user add EMAIL [--name NAME] [--role ROLE]...
homegap user password EMAIL
homegap user block EMAIL
homegap user unblock EMAIL
homegap user remove EMAIL

Manages the users of the sign-in. Run it in the orchestrator container. The command calls the dashboard API of the orchestrator in the same container, with your dashboard token or the token that HomeGAP created. Thus the orchestrator must run. See Users, machines and devices.

Action What it does list Prints one line for each user: the email address, the roles and active or blocked. add Creates the user and prints a new password. You can repeat --role. Without --role, the user gets the role Member. password Gives the user a new password and prints it. block Blocks the user. A blocked user cannot sign in, and each session of the user ends. unblock Ends the block. remove Removes the user.

HomeGAP does not keep a password. add and password print it one time:

password: <password>
HomeGAP does not keep the password. Give it to the user now.

items.title: machine
items.text:
homegap machine list
homegap machine add NAME [--role ROLE]...
homegap machine remove NAME

Manages the machines. A machine is a device with no user, for example a server that needs access. The command uses the dashboard API in the same way as homegap user.

Action What it does list Prints one line for each machine: the name, the id and the roles. add Creates the machine and prints its id and its secret. You can repeat --role. Without --role, the machine gets the role Member. remove Removes the machine.

A machine name has 1 to 60 characters: letters, digits, spaces, ., - and _. HomeGAP does not keep the secret. add prints it one time:

id: <id>
secret: <secret>
HomeGAP does not keep the secret. Give it to the machine now.

items.title: init
items.text:
homegap init [--dir PATH] [--yes] [--refresh]

Writes the files of the homelab stack to a folder. Run it in a container of its own, with your folder at /work:

docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/drewcarlson/homegap init

The command writes compose.yml, upgrade.sh and the example files. If they are missing, it also makes .env, config/config.yml and the five folders in data/. If the owner of the folder is not the user 1000:1000, it writes HOMEGAP_UID and HOMEGAP_GID to the new .env. It never changes a file of your own. See Install on the homelab.

If a file of the stack has changes from you, the command asks before it replaces the file. Each line of the output has a result and a path:

Result Meaning created The folder has no such file. The command makes it. updated The file has no changes from you. The command writes the content of this version. unchanged The file already has the content of this version. replaced Your answer is yes. Your file is now <name>.previous. kept Your answer is no, or there is no terminal. The file of this version is <name>.new. Option What it does --dir PATH The folder. The default is /work. --yes Replaces each file that has changes from you, with no question. --refresh Changes only the files of the stack. It makes no file of your own. upgrade.sh uses it.

items.title: version and help
items.text: homegap version (or --version) prints the version of the binary. homegap help (or --help, -h) prints the usage.

items.title: Exit codes and errors
items.text:
Case Result An unknown command. The command prints the usage and exits with code 2. A fatal error. The command prints homegap: <message> on stderr, and homegap: caused by ... if there is a cause. It exits with code 1.

With HOMEGAP_DEBUG set, a fatal error also prints the stack trace.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
Variable Default Use HOMEGAP_CONFIG /config/config.yml The config file. HOMEGAP_DRY_RUN None. 1, true or yes starts run in dry run. DOCKER_SOCKET /var/run/docker.sock The Docker socket that the orchestrator reads. DOCKER_HOST None. The address of a Docker API. The stack sets it to tcp://docker-proxy:2375. HOMEGAP_MESH_DIR /mesh The folder that the orchestrator and the mesh agent share. HOMEGAP_IDENTITY_DIR /identity The folder with the signed directory of users. HOMEGAP_SIGN_IN_DIR /sign-in The folder of the sign-in. HOMEGAP_VPN_DIR /vpn The folder that the sign-in and the mesh agent share. HOMEGAP_STACK_FILES /usr/share/homegap/deploy The folder in the image with the stack files, for init.

Each of the four folders has a fixed path in the image. If that path is not a folder, HomeGAP uses a folder of the same name in the data directory.

For all variables, see the Configuration reference.

items.title: Files and state
items.text: This page lists the files that HomeGAP reads and writes on the homelab and on the nodes.

items.title: The folder of the homelab stack
items.text:
Path Content compose.yml, upgrade.sh The compose file of the stack and the upgrade script. An upgrade replaces them. .env.example, compose.override.example.yml, config/config.example.yml The examples. An upgrade replaces them. .homegap/ A copy of each file that HomeGAP wrote to the folder. HomeGAP uses it to find the files that you changed. <file>.new The file of the new version, next to a file that you changed and kept. <file>.previous Your file, after you let HomeGAP replace it. .env The secrets and the variables of compose.yml, with mode 600. compose.override.yml Your changes to the stack. config/config.yml The config file. config/config.yml.bak-<epoch ms> The backups of the edits from the dashboard, with mode 0600. HomeGAP keeps the newest 10. See Configuration. data/ All that HomeGAP writes. The sections below list its folders.

HomeGAP never changes .env, compose.override.yml and config/config.yml in an upgrade. See Install on the homelab and Homelab stack.

items.title: The data directory of the orchestrator
items.text:
The data directory is data_dir (default /data). With the shipped compose file, this is the folder data/orchestrator of the stack. No other container mounts it.

Path Content state.json The state cache, with mode 0600: the slot and the mesh public key of each node, the last runs, the pauses and the ids of the Bunny zones. state.json.bak A copy of the state cache from the last start. HomeGAP uses it if state.json is damaged. state.json.corrupt A copy of a state cache that HomeGAP was not able to read. discovery.json The containers of the last discovery, with their labels. HomeGAP uses it for the grace period of a container that is gone. activity.json The activity log of the dashboard. dashboard-token The dashboard token that HomeGAP creates if the config gives none, with mode 0600. known_hosts The SSH host keys of the nodes. ssh/ The SSH keys of the nodes, with mode 0600: the keys from the add-node wizard (<id>_ed25519), and the keys that you put there by hand. ssh-askpass.sh A helper that gives the setup password to ssh. authority/authority.key The private key that signs the directory of users, with mode 0600. authority/users.json The users, the machines and the blocked devices, with mode 0600. It holds a hash of each password, not the password. acme/ The ACME account key (lego/), and the certificate of the nodes with its key (node.crt, node.key, node-cert.json). The folder also holds the state of the order and the last 20 orders. See Certificates. locations.yml Your edits to the location catalog. speedtests.json The results of the speed tests.

Warning

If state.json is damaged and there is no good copy, the orchestrator does not start. An empty state drops each pause and the slot of each node. Restore the file from a backup. Delete it only if you want an empty state.

Include the full folder in your backup. The folders authority/ and ssh/ and the file state.json have no other copy.

items.title: The shared folders of the homelab
items.text: Each of these folders has a fixed path in the HomeGAP image. The compose file mounts the folder of the stack there.

items.title: data/mesh (at /mesh)
items.text:
The orchestrator and the mesh agent share this folder.

Path Written by Content mesh.json The orchestrator The description of the mesh: the interface, the peers, the forwards and the VPN. status.json The mesh agent The public key of the homelab, the description that the agent applied and the peers that it sees. host-gateway The mesh agent The address of the homelab host, as the mesh namespace reaches it. hg-mesh.key, hg-mesh.conf The mesh agent The WireGuard key and the config of the mesh interface, with mode 0600. hg-vpn.key, hg-vpn.conf The mesh agent The WireGuard key and the config of the VPN interface, with mode 0600.

items.title: data/identity (at /identity)
items.text:
The orchestrator writes this folder after each change of a user, a machine or a private service. The sign-in reads it.

Path Content directory.json The directory of users, machines, roles and private services, with the signature of the homelab. authority.pub The public key that checks the signature.

The sign-in accepts a directory only with a valid signature. The private key stays in data/orchestrator/authority/.

items.title: data/sign-in (at /sign-in)
items.text:
Only the sign-in container writes this folder. The orchestrator reads the public key.

Path Content issuer.key The private key of the sign-in, with mode 0600. It signs the sessions of the devices. issuer.pub The public key of the sign-in. devices.json The devices that signed in, with mode 0600. ended-sessions.json The sessions that ended before their expiry.

items.title: data/vpn (at /vpn)
items.text:
The sign-in and the mesh agent share this folder. The orchestrator reads it for the Access page.

Path Written by Content peers.json The sign-in The devices that are connected. devices.json The sign-in The devices, for the nodes. directory.json The sign-in A copy of the signed directory, for the nodes. status.json The mesh agent The state of the VPN interface: its key, its port, the peers and the exits of the nodes.

See Sign-in and VPN.

items.title: The image
items.text:
Path Content /usr/local/bin/homegap The HomeGAP binary. /usr/local/bin/lego Lego, the ACME client that orders the certificate of the nodes. /usr/share/homegap/map/world.pmtiles The map tiles. /usr/share/homegap/docs These docs. /usr/share/homegap/deploy The files of the homelab stack, for homegap init.

The image creates the system user homegap (uid 10001), with the home directory /data. The Dockerfile has no USER line, so a container runs as root unless the compose file sets a user. The shipped compose file runs the orchestrator and the sign-in as the owner of the stack folder.

items.title: The node
items.text:
The stack is in node_stack.install_dir (default /opt/homegap):

Path Content compose.yml The compose file of the node stack: Traefik, the maintenance page, the agent of HomeGAP and, with node_stack.crowdsec, CrowdSec. .env The environment of the stack, with mode 0600. With CrowdSec, it holds the key of the bouncer. config/traefik/traefik_config.yml The static config of Traefik. config/traefik/dynamic/homegap-routes.yml The routes that HomeGAP writes. config/traefik/dynamic/homegap-headers.yml The middleware for the HSTS header. config/traefik/dynamic/homegap-tls.yml The file that tells Traefik where the certificate is. config/traefik/dynamic/homegap-crowdsec.yml The bouncer middleware, with mode 0600. Only with node_stack.crowdsec. config/traefik/dynamic/homegap-maintenance.yml The routes of the maintenance page. The maintenance service adds the file while the node cannot reach the homelab, and removes it after. config/traefik/certs/homegap.crt, homegap.key The certificate that HomeGAP orders, with mode 0600. The folder has mode 0700. config/traefik/logs/ The logs of Traefik. config/maintenance/ The files of the maintenance page: server.py, index.html, routes.yml and probe.json. config/crowdsec/ The config and the database of CrowdSec. Only with node_stack.crowdsec. config/homegap-sysctl.conf The TCP tuning. HomeGAP installs it as /etc/sysctl.d/99-homegap.conf. agent/agent.json What the agent of the node does: the PROXY protocol ports and the exit of the node. The agent acts when the file changes. agent-state/ The state of the agent, with mode 0700. It holds the key and the config of the exit (hg-exit.key, hg-exit.conf) and a copy of the signed directory (identity/). It also holds the key of the sign-in of the node (control/). .homegap-rollback The saved stack, during an update. It has mode 0700.

HomeGAP reverts a manual edit of a file that it writes here.

HomeGAP also writes these files on the node:

Path Content /etc/wireguard/hg-mesh.conf The config of the mesh interface, with mode 0600. /etc/wireguard/hg-mesh.key The mesh key of the node. The node creates it, and the private key never leaves the node. /etc/wireguard/hg-mesh-forwards.sh The rules that forward the raw ports to the homelab. /etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d/10-homegap-mesh.conf Starts Docker after the mesh interface. /etc/sysctl.d/99-homegap.conf The TCP tuning of the host, with node_stack.tcp_tuning. /etc/docker/daemon.json The log limit of 30 MB for each container. HomeGAP writes it only when it installs Docker and the file does not exist. /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/01-homegap.conf The SSH hardening from the add-node wizard. /etc/sudoers.d/90-homegap-<user> The sudo rule of the SSH user, from the add-node wizard.

When you decommission a node, HomeGAP stops the stack and removes the install folder with its data. It also removes the mesh interface, its config and the forward rules.

items.title: Glossary
items.text:
This page defines the terms that the HomeGAP docs use.

Agent of a node The homegap-agent container on a node (homegap node-agent). It serves the raw TCP ports with PROXY protocol and the exit of the node. During an outage of the homelab, it also serves the sign-in. Bunny DNS The DNS service of bunny.net. It sends each viewer to the nearest healthy node. See DNS routing and health checks. Desired state The Docker labels and the config file, and nothing else. The orchestrator moves the actual state toward it. See How HomeGAP works. Device One app that signed in, or one machine. A device has a WireGuard key and an address in the VPN. You can block, unblock or delete it. See Users, machines and devices. Directory The list of users, machines, roles, private names and blocks. The orchestrator signs it, and the sign-in and the nodes trust only a directory with that signature. See Security model. Drift A change on a node that HomeGAP did not make. The node check repairs it. See Node updates and rollback. Exit A way to the internet for a VPN device. Exit via <node> leaves with the address of that node, and Exit via homelab leaves from home. See Exit nodes and tunnel DNS. Extra domain A domain for services in addition to domain, from extra_domains in the config file. See Extra domains. Front door The homelab Traefik container with the root domain in homegap.expose. It claims the root and, with homegap.wildcard, *.<domain>. Each extra domain can have its own front door. See Services. Geo record set A set of DNS records for one name, one for each node, with geo routing and a health monitor. See DNS routing and health checks. Homelab The home servers with Docker, the homelab Traefik and the services. It has no inbound ports. Machine A device with no user, for example a server that needs access. It signs in with an id and a secret. See Users, machines and devices. Maintenance page The page that a node shows while it cannot reach the homelab. The homegap-maintenance container of the node serves it. Management host The name of one node, node-<id>.<domain>. See Manage nodes. Mesh The private WireGuard network hg-mesh between the homelab and every node. It is always on, and every route from a node to the homelab goes over it. See Mesh. Mesh agent The homegap-mesh-agent container on the homelab (homegap mesh). It keeps the mesh interface, the home end of the VPN and the firewall of the mesh namespace. Mesh namespace The network namespace of the homegap-mesh container on the homelab. The mesh interface and the interface of the VPN devices are there, and the orchestrator is not. See Security model. Named service A service under homegap.services.<name>. on a container that can also have other services. Its key is <host slug>--<name>. See Labels. Node A VPS that runs Traefik, the maintenance page and the agent of HomeGAP. Node ids are like na1, eu1 and as1. See Prepare the servers. Olm The command line client of the Pangolin apps. A machine connects with it. Orchestrator The homegap run process on the homelab. It reads the labels and manages the nodes, the mesh, the users and DNS. It is never in the traffic path of your services. It serves only its own pages: the dashboard and, if enabled, the status page and the speed test. Pangolin apps The unmodified Pangolin apps for Android, iOS and desktop. A user connects a device to the VPN with one of them. See Connect the Pangolin apps. Pass One run of the reconcile loop. See How HomeGAP works. Passthrough The TLS mode where the node reads only the SNI and forwards the encrypted stream to the homelab. See Traffic paths. Port list A list of raw ports in homegap.port, with entries like 7881/tcp, 3478/tcp+udp or 2222:22/tcp. See Labels. Private path A route that only VPN devices use to reach a public service, over a separate Docker network. See Client addresses and private-only services. Private service A service with homegap.access: private. It gets a name that only VPN devices resolve and reach. See Private services. Role A name that connects users and machines to private services and exits. Admin and Member always exist, and you can name more. A private service with no homegap.roles label is for Admin only. Rollout An update of the node stacks, one node at a time. See Node updates and rollback. Sign-in The homegap-sign-in container on the homelab (homegap sign-in). A user signs in there with a HomeGAP password or through an OpenID Connect provider. sign_in.url is its address, and each node serves it. See Sign-in. Slot The permanent number of a node. It gives the mesh address of the node. See Manage nodes. Terminate The TLS mode where the node ends TLS, with the certificate that HomeGAP orders for the nodes. See Traffic paths. Tunnel DNS The DNS servers of vpn.tunnel_dns. An app with "DNS over tunnel" sends its lookups to them through the VPN. See Exit nodes and tunnel DNS. User A person who can sign in. A user has an email address, a name, roles and an optional password. See Users, machines and devices. VPN The WireGuard connection of a device to the homelab. The device connects to a node, and the node forwards the packets over the mesh. The node cannot read them.

items.title: The mesh
items.text: The mesh is the private WireGuard network between the homelab and each node. This page tells you how its addresses, keys and firewall work and what the mesh agent does. It also tells you how to read the mesh view of the dashboard.

items.title: What the mesh is
items.text:
hg-mesh is a WireGuard interface on the homelab and on each node. Each member is a peer of all other members. The mesh is always on, and each route from a node to the homelab goes over it: web traffic, raw ports, the sign-in and the VPN of the devices.

mesh:
  subnet: 10.77.0.0/24
  port: 51821
Key Default Rules mesh.subnet 10.77.0.0/24 An IPv4 network address with a prefix from /16 to /26. It must not overlap 100.64.0.0/10, where the VPN has its addresses. mesh.port 51821 The UDP port that each node listens on.

items.title: Addresses and slots
items.text:
The addresses do not change. The homelab is host 1 of mesh.subnet. A node is host 10 + slot.

Member Address (default subnet) The homelab 10.77.0.1 The node with slot 0 10.77.0.10 The node with slot 1 10.77.0.11

The slot of a node is permanent. HomeGAP keeps the slots in its state, so a node keeps its address when other nodes go or change their order in the config. A new node gets the lowest free slot. A node that waits for its removal keeps its slot until the removal ends. There are 32 slots, thus the maximum is 32 nodes.

The slot also gives the node its exit address in the VPN. See Exits and tunnel DNS.

items.title: Keys
items.text:
Each node makes its own key during its first setup, in /etc/wireguard/hg-mesh.key. The private key stays on the node. HomeGAP learns only the public key, from the output of the setup script.

The mesh agent of the homelab makes the key of the homelab one time, in the folder data/mesh. Only the owner of the file can read it. The key does not go to the orchestrator.

items.title: Connections
items.text:
The homelab has no public endpoint. It dials each node and sends a keepalive every 25 seconds. Thus the mesh works behind NAT, and no DNS record publishes your home address.

The nodes connect to each other directly, on their public addresses and mesh.port. Each peer has only the one mesh address of the other member as its permitted address.

items.title: The interface of a node
items.text:
On a node, wg-quick manages the interface from /etc/wireguard/hg-mesh.conf. Where systemd runs, the interface starts at boot.

In each pass, the orchestrator runs the mesh script on each node over SSH. The script installs wireguard-tools, writes the peer list and applies peer changes in place with wg syncconf. The current sessions stay. If a node joins with a new key, a second round in the same pass gives that key to the other members. On a paused node, the orchestrator only reads the state.

The same pass writes the forward rules of the node, in /etc/wireguard/hg-mesh-forwards.sh. The interface also runs this script at boot.

items.title: The mesh agent of the homelab
items.text:
On the homelab, the interface is in the network namespace of the homegap-mesh container. That container has a fixed image and does nothing but hold the namespace. The orchestrator is not in it.

The homegap-mesh-agent container runs homegap mesh in that namespace, with the capabilities NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW and DAC_OVERRIDE. It is the only container there that can change the network. The orchestrator and the agent talk through files in data/mesh:

File Writer Content mesh.json The orchestrator The description of the mesh: the address, the peers, the forwards and the VPN. status.json The agent The public key of the homelab, the description that is in effect, the state of each peer and the last error. host-gateway The agent The address of the homelab host, as the namespace reaches it.

The agent does these jobs:

  • It keeps hg-mesh as mesh.json describes it. It applies a change of the file at once.
  • It keeps the forwards. A forward sends one port of the mesh address of the homelab to one container: the front door or a service.
  • It keeps hg-vpn, the home end of the VPN, and the firewall rules of each connected device. See Sign-in and VPN.
  • It sends each node the devices for the exit of that node, with the signed directory. See Exits and tunnel DNS.
  • It writes status.json every 15 seconds, and it applies the full description again every 60 seconds. This repairs a rule or a peer that is not as the description says.

The agent installs the firewall before it starts the interface. If the firewall fails, the mesh stays down and never open.

upgrade.sh recreates the mesh agent with each upgrade, and the interface stays up without it. The script recreates homegap-mesh only when its part of the compose files changes. The mesh is then down for a few seconds. See Upgrade.

items.title: On a node
items.text:
The firewall of the node (ufw) opens mesh.port/udp to each address. WireGuard authenticates each packet, and the address of the homelab can change. ufw opens no port of the node on the mesh interface.

HomeGAP keeps its own chains before the chains of ufw and of Docker:

  • HG-RAW, HG-RAW-FWD and HG-RAW-NAT forward the raw ports of your services, and the port of the VPN, to the homelab over the mesh. The homelab sees the mesh address of the node as the source.
  • HG-RAW-IN accepts the PROXY protocol ports that the agent of the node serves.
  • HG-EXIT-IN, HG-EXIT-FWD and HG-EXIT-NAT are the firewall of the exit of the node.

The agent of the node listens on two ports of its mesh address:

Port Use Source that the firewall accepts 8091/tcp The device list from the homelab. The mesh address of the homelab only. 8092/tcp The sign-in of the node, for the time that the homelab is down. The Docker networks of the node only, where the Traefik of the node is.

items.title: On the homelab
items.text:
Each node is a member of the mesh, so HomeGAP treats the namespace of homegap-mesh as reachable from the nodes. The agent keeps a firewall there (the chains HG-IN, HG-OUT, HG-FWD, HG-NAT and HG-DNAT) that refuses everything except these connections:

  • Into the namespace: answers, ping, WireGuard of the VPN from a node over the mesh, and the probe of a device.
  • Out of the namespace: the mesh, answers and WireGuard to the nodes.
  • Through the namespace, from a node: only the forwards, each to its one container.
  • Through the namespace, from a device: only what the roles of its user permit.
  • Through the namespace, from the orchestrator: to the members over the mesh.

Thus a node or a container in that namespace cannot open a connection to the orchestrator, to your other containers or to your home network. See Security model.

items.title: The mesh view of the dashboard
items.text:
The Nodes page shows the mesh in two places.

The Mesh link column of the Nodes table shows link up or link down for each node.

The Mesh panel is a matrix. Each row is a member, and each column is a peer of that member. The note next to the title gives the number of links that are up, for example "6 of 6 links". A cell shows the time since the last WireGuard handshake of the member with the peer. WireGuard does a new handshake approximately every 2 minutes while traffic flows.

Cell Tooltip Meaning Green None. The last handshake is 3 minutes old or less. Amber "No recent handshake" The last handshake is 3 to 10 minutes old. Rose "No handshake for over 10 minutes" The last handshake is more than 10 minutes old. Rose, never "No handshake yet" The member has no handshake with the peer yet. Rose, not configured "Not in this member's peer list yet" The member does not have this peer in its configuration yet. Dim "This member could not be read" HomeGAP cannot read the state of the member.

If a link stays down, check that the firewall of your server provider lets mesh.port/udp reach the node. The log of the orchestrator has the error of a member one time, and "mesh is healthy again" after the recovery. For the logs of the agent, run docker compose logs homegap-mesh-agent on the homelab.

items.title: Ports and firewall
items.text: This page lists the ports that HomeGAP uses on the nodes and on the homelab.

items.title: Node: public ports
items.text:
With firewall: true (the default), HomeGAP opens these ports in ufw:

Port Use ssh_port/tcp (default 22) SSH, from anywhere or only from ssh_allow_from. 80/tcp HTTP: the health probe of Bunny and the redirects to HTTPS. 443/tcp HTTPS. 443/udp UDP on the HTTPS port (HTTP/3). mesh.port/udp (default 51821) The mesh. WireGuard authenticates each packet.

HomeGAP opens the next ports in its own iptables chains, before the rules of ufw. Thus the firewall follows a new port at once.

Port Use vpn.port/udp (default 51830) The VPN. The kernel of the node forwards the packets over the mesh to the homelab. vpn.exit_port/udp (default 51840) The exit of the node, with vpn.exit_nodes.nodes: true. The public ports of raw services Raw TCP and UDP services, as their labels set them. The kernel forwards them over the mesh. The public ports of raw TCP services with homegap.proxy_protocol The agent of the node accepts them and adds the PROXY protocol header.

A firewall at the provider level must open the same ports.

items.title: Node: ports that the internet cannot reach
items.text:
Port Where Use 8091/tcp The mesh address of the node, with vpn.exit_nodes.nodes: true The agent takes the devices of its exit from the homelab. The firewall accepts only the mesh address of the homelab. 8092/tcp The mesh address of the node, with vpn.exit_nodes.nodes: true and sign_in.url The sign-in of the node for an outage of the homelab. The firewall accepts only a Docker network of the node, where its Traefik is. vpn.exit_port + 1/udp The exit address of the node, inside the VPN The liveness probe of a device. 8090/tcp The homegap-maintenance container The maintenance page. The container publishes no port, so only the Traefik of the node reaches it. 127.0.0.1:8082 The traefik container The metrics of Traefik. The orchestrator reads them through SSH.

ufw opens no port on the mesh interface.

items.title: Node: reserved ports
items.text:
A public raw service cannot use these ports on a node:

  • 80 and 443, for the web.
  • 8091 and 8092, for the agent of the node.
  • The SSH port of each node that serves the service (ssh_port, default 22).
  • mesh.port/udp.

HomeGAP refuses such a service and reports a label error. Publish the service on a different port.

A public service cannot take vpn.port/udp, vpn.exit_port/udp or the port after each of them. HomeGAP refuses the service and shows a label error.

items.title: Homelab
items.text:
The homelab has no inbound ports from the internet. The mesh agent dials each node.

Port Where Use dashboard.bind (8088) The orchestrator container. The stack publishes it on 127.0.0.1:8088 of the host. The dashboard. Reach it only privately. speedtest.bind (8089) The orchestrator container The public origin of the speed test and the status page. Your Traefik routes to it, with the route that HomeGAP gives it through the HTTP provider. 8090/tcp The homegap-sign-in container The sign-in. Each node sends the name of sign_in.url to it over the mesh. From node_stack.mesh_port_base (default 40000) The mesh address of the homelab One port for each service that a node reaches by name. The mesh namespace forwards it to the container. No node publishes these ports. The public ports of raw services The mesh address of the homelab The mesh namespace forwards each port to its container. vpn.port/udp (default 51830) The mesh address of the homelab The WireGuard peer of the VPN. It accepts packets only from the mesh. vpn.port + 1/udp The VPN address of the homelab, inside the VPN The liveness probe of a device. 2375/tcp The docker-proxy container The read-only Docker API. Only the orchestrator reaches it. 8080 on your Traefik Your front door container The Traefik API, with api.insecure: true, for homegap.private_middleware. Do not publish it.

items.title: Addresses
items.text:
Range Use Host 1 of mesh.subnet (default 10.77.0.0/24) The mesh address of the homelab. Host 10 + slot of mesh.subnet The mesh address of a node. The first address of vpn.client_subnet (default 100.90.0.0/16) The VPN address of the homelab. The last 256 addresses of vpn.client_subnet The exit addresses of the nodes. No device gets one. vpn.utility_subnet (default 100.96.128.0/24) The DNS proxy of the apps and the addresses of private names.

See Mesh and Manage nodes.

items.title: Security model
items.text: This page tells you where HomeGAP keeps its secrets, what each part can reach and what the public can see.

items.title: The orchestrator is the trust center
items.text:
The orchestrator holds every SSH key, the Bunny API key and the key that signs the directory of users. Thus:

  • Run it on a minimal host.
  • Mount the secrets. Do not put them in the image.
  • Keep the dashboard private. Every /api route needs the dashboard token or a sign-in through dashboard.sso, with two exceptions. The terminal WebSocket needs a one-time ticket. The Traefik of the homelab reads /api/traefik/homelab from the front door container. Set your own token with dashboard.auth_token_env. An address that sends more than 20 wrong tokens in one minute gets the answer 429 until that minute ends. For a request that the front door forwards, the address is the address of the viewer, so one viewer cannot lock a different viewer out. The dashboard loads only its own files, and no other page can show it in a frame.

Warning

If somebody gets access to the dashboard or to the orchestrator host, that person has control of every node and of every user.

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
HomeGAP makes its keys and tokens from the CSPRNG of the kernel. Each key stays in the container that made it:

Secret Where it is Who can read it The SSH keys of the nodes, the state cache and the dashboard token data/orchestrator The orchestrator. The key that signs the directory of users (authority.key) data/orchestrator/authority The orchestrator. The mesh key and the VPN key of the homelab data/mesh (mode 0600) The mesh agent. The key that signs the sessions (issuer.key) data/sign-in The sign-in. The mesh key of a node /etc/wireguard on the node Root on the node. The key of the exit of a node agent-state in the install directory of the node The agent of the node. The CrowdSec bouncer key of a node The state cache, and .env on the node (mode 0600) The orchestrator and the node.

The local state file /data/state.json has mode 0600. The add-node wizard keeps a setup password in memory for the job only. It never stores it. HomeGAP writes generated node keys to the data directory with mode 0600.

HomeGAP does not keep a password of a user or a secret of a machine. It shows each one time and keeps only a hash.

See Secrets.

items.title: Access to the nodes
items.text:
The orchestrator controls a node only through SSH. The add-node wizard sends a password only to a host key that you confirmed. After that, HomeGAP connects to a node only if it shows the host key from its first connection.

The dashboard can open a shell on a node. See The dashboard. The shell uses the SSH connection of the orchestrator, so the key stays on the homelab. A WebSocket carries the terminal. It accepts only a single-use ticket from the API, and only from the page of the dashboard. dashboard.terminal: false turns the feature off.

ufw on the node opens only the ports in Ports and firewall. HomeGAP adds new rules before it removes its old rules. It never touches rules that it did not add. The raw ports, the VPN port and the exit port are in chains of HomeGAP itself, before the rules of ufw.

The agent of a node (homegap-agent) is in the network of the host. It is root with a read-only file system and four capabilities: NET_BIND_SERVICE, NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW and DAC_OVERRIDE. It holds no SSH key, no DNS key and no Docker access.

items.title: The homelab
items.text:
Each container of the homelab stack has only the rights that its job needs:

Container User Capabilities Network orchestrator The owner of the stack folder None. The Traefik network and the network of the Docker proxy. homegap-sign-in The owner of the stack folder None. Its file system is read-only. The Traefik network. homegap-mesh-agent Root NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW, DAC_OVERRIDE The namespace of homegap-mesh. homegap-mesh Root The defaults of Docker. It runs only sleep. The network homegap-mesh and the Traefik network. docker-proxy Root The defaults of Docker. The network of the Docker proxy, which has no way out.

Every container except homegap-mesh and docker-proxy has no-new-privileges.

items.title: The Docker socket
items.text:
The orchestrator has no Docker socket. It reads Docker through the docker-proxy service, which accepts only GET requests for the containers and the events. Only the orchestrator can reach the proxy.

Warning

Do not mount the Docker socket in the orchestrator. A socket mount gives the full Docker API, also with :ro. A person who controls that container then controls the Docker host.

items.title: The sign-in
items.text: The sign-in is the part of the homelab that the internet reaches. It is a container of its own, so it has no SSH key, no DNS key and no Docker access. It mounts the config and the directory of users read-only. Only the orchestrator mounts the folder data/orchestrator.

items.title: The mesh namespace
items.text:
Each node is a member of the mesh, so HomeGAP treats the mesh namespace as reachable from the nodes. The orchestrator is not in it. The mesh agent is the only container there that can change the network. It loads the firewall before it starts an interface, so a failure leaves the mesh down and never open. The firewall refuses all traffic, with these exceptions:

  • In: answers, ping, the WireGuard packets of VPN devices from a node, and the liveness probe of a device.
  • Out: the mesh, answers, and WireGuard to the nodes. Nothing in the namespace can open a connection to the orchestrator, to a different container or to your home network.
  • From a node: only the ports of the published services, each to its one container.
  • From a VPN device: only the private services that a role of its user permits. A rule names the address of the device, and WireGuard accepts that address only from the key of the device.

A device that uses "Exit via homelab" reaches the internet from the namespace. It reaches no private address range and not the mesh. See Mesh.

HomeGAP never publishes the IP address of the homelab. The homelab dials the mesh, so it has no inbound port from the internet.

items.title: Users and sign-in
items.text:
