The orchestrator is the authority for users. It keeps the users, the machines, the roles and the block lists, and it signs them as one directory. The sign-in and each node trust only a directory with that signature, and they never accept an older version.

  • Passwords: HomeGAP stores a password as a PBKDF2-SHA256 hash with 600,000 iterations and its own salt. A password has 12 characters or more.
  • Secrets of machines and devices: HomeGAP stores only the SHA-256 of each secret.
  • Sessions: the sign-in signs each session token with its own key. The directory names that key, and only such a session gives access to the homelab. A session of a user lasts 30 days. The token for the control connection of a device lasts 7 days.
  • Limits: after five wrong passwords in 15 minutes, the sign-in refuses the address of the browser and the email address. A sign-in code lasts 10 minutes.
  • Blocks: a block of a user or a device goes into the signed directory. The session of a blocked user gives no access, and the device loses its connection.

With sign_in.oidc, the provider proves the email address of the user, with its own second factor. The user must exist in HomeGAP, and HomeGAP gives the roles. See Sign-in.

items.title: What a node holds and can do
items.text:
A node is a server at a provider, so HomeGAP gives it as little as possible. A node holds:

  • The certificate of the nodes and its key, for the names that the nodes terminate.
  • Its own mesh key and, with vpn.exit_nodes.nodes, the key of its exit.
  • The public key of the homelab.
  • With vpn.exit_nodes.nodes, the signed directory and the list of devices. They contain the password hashes of the users and the hashes of the secrets.

A node holds no SSH key, no Bunny key and no key that signs for the homelab. It cannot make a user, a role or a session that the homelab accepts. Into the homelab, it reaches only the ports of the published services.

During an outage of the homelab, a node with an exit signs devices in itself, with a HomeGAP password. It signs such a session with its own key, which the directory does not name. Thus the session gives the exit of that node and nothing at home. The firewall of the node accepts this sign-in only from a Docker network of the node, where its Traefik is. A block during an outage reaches a node only after the homelab is back.

Warning

A node ends TLS for the name of the sign-in. A person with root on a node can read the passwords that users type there. That person can also read the session tokens of the devices that connect through it. With a token, that person can act as its user, with the rights of that user, until you block the user. The password hashes on a node are also open to an offline attack. Use sign_in.oidc with a second factor, and rent nodes only from providers that you trust.

A node cannot read the VPN traffic to the homelab. WireGuard encrypts it from the device to the mesh namespace, and the node only forwards the packets.

items.title: Images
items.text:
The default images of Traefik, CrowdSec and the maintenance page have a version tag. A node gets a new version of them only when the default or your config changes. The agent of a node runs the HomeGAP image. Its tag is the value of HOMEGAP_VERSION. Without that variable, the tag is the version of the orchestrator. See Node updates and rollback.

The release build signs the HomeGAP image. HomeGAP does not check a signature before it uses an image. To check the image yourself, see Upgrade the homelab.

items.title: Traffic
items.text:
With passthrough, a node cannot read the traffic. It holds no certificate for a passthrough name. With the CAA records of the domain, it cannot order one. A node can see the name, the address of the client, and the size and time of the traffic.

A node can read the traffic of each name that it terminates. These are the name of the sign-in, the shared names of the status page and the speed test, and each service with homegap.tls: terminate. A front door with terminate and homegap.wildcard gives the nodes all web traffic of the domain. See Certificates.

The nodes send an HSTS header on each name that they terminate. A browser then uses only HTTPS for that name for one year.

node_stack.crowdsec gives abuse mitigation on the edge for terminated traffic only. It cannot examine passthrough streams.

items.title: Calls to outside services
items.text:
The software that HomeGAP runs makes no calls home of its own. On the Traefik of each node, HomeGAP turns off the version check and the usage data.

The system needs the calls that remain:

  • The orchestrator calls the Bunny API for the DNS records.
  • The orchestrator orders the certificate of the nodes from Let's Encrypt. The nodes order no certificates.
  • With sign_in.oidc, the sign-in calls your provider.
  • With node_stack.crowdsec, Traefik on the nodes downloads the CrowdSec bouncer plugin from the Traefik plugin catalog when it starts. CrowdSec talks to its central API for the community blocklists.

You configure your own Traefik on the homelab. Set global.checkNewVersion and global.sendAnonymousUsage to false in its static configuration to turn off the same calls there.

items.title: What the public can see
items.text:
• The public status page shows the id, the region, the state and the location of each node. It also uses the name status-<node>.<domain> of each node, which resolves to the public address of that node. It shows the homelab only as its region. Only a VPN device, which gets the page over the private path, sees the location of the homelab. Each visitor sees only the address of that visitor. See Status page.
  • The token of a speed test link for a device is in the fragment of the URL. Thus it is never part of a request URL, and no access log contains it. The test page sends it in a header. With speedtest.vpn_access: true, each VPN device that can use the private path of the front door gets a link with no action from you. See Speed tests.
  • The nodes end TLS for the shared names status.<domain> and speedtest.<domain>, which serve only these HomeGAP pages. A node then sends each request back into its own port 443 under its own name, and the front door carries it home still encrypted. On that inner connection the node does not check the certificate, because the connection does not leave the node before it enters the mesh.

items.title: Report a security issue
items.text: To report a security issue, open a private security advisory on GitHub at https://github.com/DrewCarlson/HomeGAP/security/advisories/new. Do not open a public issue.

items.title: Homelab stack
items.text: This page describes the stack that homegap init writes to the homelab: the variables of .env, the image tags, your changes to the stack, the networks, the data folder and the services. To install the stack, see Install on the homelab.

items.title: The files
items.text:
The stack is one Docker Compose project with the name homegap. Three files configure it:

File What it holds Who changes it compose.yml The services, the networks and the mounts. HomeGAP. upgrade.sh replaces it with the file of the new version. Do not edit it. .env The secrets and the variables of compose.yml. You. compose.override.yml Each other change to the stack. You. upgrade.sh never changes it.

items.title: Variables in .env
items.text:
Variable Default What it sets BUNNY_API_KEY None. It is necessary. The API key of your Bunny account. HOMEGAP_DASHBOARD_TOKEN Empty. The bearer token of the dashboard. If it is empty, HomeGAP creates a token. TRAEFIK_NETWORK traefik The name of the Docker network of your Traefik. HOMEGAP_DATA_DIR ./data The folder of all that HomeGAP writes. HOMEGAP_VERSION latest The tag of the HomeGAP image. The agent of each node runs the same version. See The image tags. HOMEGAP_UID, HOMEGAP_GID 1000 The user and the group of the orchestrator and the sign-in: the owner of the stack folder. HOMEGAP_DASHBOARD_PUBLISH 127.0.0.1:8088 The address and the port of the host that publish the dashboard. HOMEGAP_DRY_RUN Empty. With true, the orchestrator runs in dry run. HOMEGAP_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET Empty. The client secret of the OpenID Connect provider of the sign-in (sign_in.oidc).

Give .env mode 600, and never commit it. homegap init creates the file from .env.example with that mode.

The orchestrator gets each variable of .env. Thus a secret that the config refers to with an *_env key needs only a line in .env. The sign-in container gets only HOMEGAP_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET. See Secrets.

items.title: The image tags
items.text:
The orchestrator, the mesh agent and the sign-in use one image, ghcr.io/drewcarlson/homegap. Each release has four tags. The tags have no v at the start.

Tag What an upgrade gets latest The newest release. 0 The newest release of major version 0. 0.1 The newest patch release of version 0.1. 0.1.0 Only this release.

To stay on one line of releases, set HOMEGAP_VERSION in .env, for example HOMEGAP_VERSION=0.1. To upgrade, see Upgrade.

items.title: Changes in compose.override.yml
items.text:
Docker Compose reads compose.override.yml after compose.yml and merges the two files. You give no extra argument. The file compose.override.example.yml has an example of each usual change. All of them attach the homegap-mesh service to a network:

services:
  homegap-mesh:
    networks:
      # A fixed address on the Traefik network, for homegap.proxy_protocol on the front door.
      traefik: { ipv4_address: 172.32.0.250 }
      # The private path (homegap.private_network on the front door).
      homegap-private: {}
      # The network of a service that HomeGAP exposes directly.
      other-stack: {}

networks:
  homegap-private:
    ipam: { config: [ { subnet: 172.33.0.0/24 } ] }
  other-stack:
    name: other_default
    external: true

Keep only the parts that you need. The nodes reach each service through the network namespace of homegap-mesh. Thus homegap-mesh must share a Docker network with each service that is not on the Traefik network.

Caution

A change to the homegap-mesh service recreates its container. The mesh agent restarts with it, and the mesh is down for a few seconds.

items.title: The networks
items.text:
Network Members Purpose traefik orchestrator, homegap-mesh, homegap-sign-in Your existing Traefik network. It is external. Its name is the value of TRAEFIK_NETWORK. homegap-docker orchestrator, docker-proxy The path of the orchestrator to the Docker socket proxy. It is internal, and no other container is on it. homegap-mesh homegap-mesh The path of the mesh namespace to the nodes. For a device that uses the homelab as its exit, it is also the path to the internet.

The homegap-mesh-agent service has no network of its own. It is in the network namespace of homegap-mesh.

items.title: The data folder
items.text:
Everything that HomeGAP writes is in folders below HOMEGAP_DATA_DIR (default ./data, next to compose.yml). The stack has no named volume. homegap init and upgrade.sh make the folders, with you as their owner.

Path Content Mounted by data/orchestrator/ The data of the orchestrator: its state, the SSH keys of the nodes, the key that signs the directory of users, the ACME account and the dashboard token. It has mode 0700. orchestrator only, at /data. data/mesh/ What the orchestrator and the mesh agent tell each other, and the WireGuard keys of the homelab. orchestrator and homegap-mesh-agent, at /mesh. data/identity/ The signed directory of users, machines and private services. orchestrator at /identity. homegap-sign-in at /identity, read-only. data/sign-in/ The key and the devices of the sign-in. homegap-sign-in at /sign-in. orchestrator at /sign-in, read-only. data/vpn/ The devices that are connected, between the sign-in and the mesh agent. homegap-sign-in and homegap-mesh-agent at /vpn. orchestrator at /vpn, read-only.

To keep the data in a different place, for example on a different disk, set HOMEGAP_DATA_DIR in .env. For each file in these folders, see Files and state.

The paths /mesh, /identity, /sign-in and /vpn are fixed in the HomeGAP image. You set no variable for them. If a shared directory is not a mount, the other container cannot see it. Then the orchestrator writes an error with the path and the name of the folder to its log.

items.title: The services
items.text:
The stack has five services. The file limits the log of each service to 30 MB.

Service Image What it does homegap-mesh docker.io/library/busybox:1.37 Holds the network namespace of the mesh. homegap-mesh-agent The HomeGAP image, with the command mesh. Keeps the mesh interface, the forwards to the containers and the home end of the VPN. orchestrator The HomeGAP image, with the command run. Reads the labels, configures the nodes and DNS, and serves the dashboard. homegap-sign-in The HomeGAP image, with the command sign-in. The public sign-in: the page where a user signs in, and the calls of the apps. docker-proxy docker.io/tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:v0.5.0 A filter in front of the Docker socket.

items.title: homegap-mesh
items.text:
The service does no work itself. It holds a network namespace with two WireGuard interfaces: hg-mesh, the mesh to the nodes, and hg-vpn, the interface of the VPN devices. Nothing else is in the namespace. The service enables IP forwarding (net.ipv4.ip_forward) in the namespace, because it forwards packets between the mesh, the devices and the containers of the services.

Each node is a member of the mesh. Thus HomeGAP treats this namespace as a place that a node can reach. The orchestrator is not in it. The firewall of the mesh agent closes the namespace. Nothing in it can open a connection to the orchestrator, to a different container or to your home network. For a node, the namespace forwards only the ports of the published services, each to its one container. For a device, it forwards only to the services that the roles of its user can use.

The service uses a fixed image, not the HomeGAP image. A new container replaces the namespace and drops the mesh, so the container must not change with a HomeGAP release. See The mesh.

items.title: homegap-mesh-agent
items.text:
The agent is the only container in the namespace of homegap-mesh that can change the network. It drops all capabilities and adds NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW and DAC_OVERRIDE. It runs as root and the folder data/mesh belongs to the user of the orchestrator, so it needs DAC_OVERRIDE.

It mounts data/mesh at /mesh and data/vpn at /vpn. If homegap-mesh gets a new container, Docker Compose restarts the agent.

items.title: orchestrator
items.text:
The orchestrator is not root. It runs as the user HOMEGAP_UID:HOMEGAP_GID, which is 1000:1000 without the two variables. Thus the files that it writes in config/ and data/ belong to you. If the owner of the stack folder is a different user, homegap init writes the two variables to .env. The orchestrator has no capability, and no-new-privileges is on.

The service publishes the dashboard on port 8088 of the loopback address of the host. To change the address, set HOMEGAP_DASHBOARD_PUBLISH. To serve the dashboard through your Traefik, set dashboard.hostname in the config.

The compose file sets these environment variables:

  • BUNNY_API_KEY. It is necessary. Docker Compose does not start the stack without it.
  • HOMEGAP_DASHBOARD_TOKEN. The bearer token of the dashboard. If it is empty, HomeGAP creates a token.
  • DOCKER_HOST. The address of docker-proxy, tcp://docker-proxy:2375.
  • HOMEGAP_DRY_RUN. It is optional.
  • Each other variable of .env.

The orchestrator mounts these folders:

  • ./config at /config. The config file is config.yml in it. This mount must be writable, unless you set dashboard.allow_config_edits: false. The mount is the folder and not the file, so an editor that replaces the file does not break it.
  • data/orchestrator at /data.
  • data/mesh at /mesh, and data/identity at /identity.
  • data/sign-in at /sign-in and data/vpn at /vpn, both read-only.

The orchestrator does not mount the Docker socket. It is on two networks: traefik and homegap-docker.

The speed test and the status page need no labels on this service. The Traefik of your homelab gets their routes from the orchestrator, at http://orchestrator:8088/api/traefik/homelab.

items.title: homegap-sign-in
items.text:
The sign-in is the part of HomeGAP that the internet reaches. For this reason it is a container of its own. It has no SSH key, no DNS key and no access to Docker. It runs as the same user as the orchestrator, with no capability and a read-only root file system. It is only on the traefik network.

It mounts these folders:

  • ./config at /config, read-only. It reads the sign_in and vpn parts of the config at its start. After a change of these parts, start the service again.
  • data/identity at /identity, read-only. It reads the signed directory of users there.
  • data/sign-in at /sign-in. It keeps its own key and the devices there.
  • data/vpn at /vpn. It writes the devices that are connected there, for the mesh agent.

Its only variable is HOMEGAP_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET. Each node sends the name of the sign-in (sign_in.url) to this container, on port 8090. See Sign-in.

items.title: docker-proxy
items.text:
The service mounts the Docker socket and accepts only GET requests for containers and events. A mount of the socket gives the whole Docker API, and with it control of the host. The orchestrator needs only to read, so the proxy refuses each other request. The service is only on the homegap-docker network, so only the orchestrator reaches it.

See Security model.

items.title: Services
items.text: This page tells you how HomeGAP publishes the services of your homelab, and when a service needs its own labels.

items.title: Labels are the source of truth
items.text: The orchestrator reads the homegap.* labels of your containers from Docker. It reads through the docker-proxy service, which refuses each request that changes something. The orchestrator never writes labels. When a container starts, stops or changes, the Docker event starts a pass at once. The debounce is reconcile.debounce (default 2s).

items.title: Most services need no labels
items.text:
The front door carries the root and every name one label under your domain. The front door is the homelab Traefik container with the root domain in homegap.expose and homegap.wildcard: "true". To publish a service through the front door, add a normal Traefik router at home.

HomeGAP treats a service as the front door when its homegap.expose is equal to domain and its access is public. A raw service is never the front door. Each extra domain can have a front door of its own. See Extra domains.

items.title: When a service needs labels
items.text:
Label a container only when it needs its own path:

  • A dedicated hostname. The service gets its own route on the nodes and its own DNS record set. This route has priority over the wildcard. See Traffic paths.
  • Raw TCP or UDP ports. See Raw TCP and UDP.
  • A private service, for the devices of the VPN only. See Private services.
  • Only some of the nodes serve the service. Use homegap.regions for this.

For all labels, see the Label reference. For the real addresses of viewers and for names that only VPN devices can open, see Client addresses and private-only services.

HomeGAP has no sign-in for a public service. To put a sign-in in front of a public service, use a forward-auth middleware on the Traefik of the homelab.

items.title: Several services on one container
items.text: One container can declare more than one service, with named services under homegap.services.<name>.. For example, a voice server can have a port list on one name and a second service with a different public port. See Named services.

items.title: Who can claim a hostname
items.text:
Only one http or https service can claim a hostname. If two containers have the same homegap.expose, the first container in the order of names wins. Each other container gets this error:

hostname <name> is already claimed by <container>

Raw services can share a hostname with each other, and with one http or https service. On the nodes that they share, only one public service can use a public port and protocol. See Shared hostnames and ports.

items.title: How HomeGAP finds the container
items.text:
Each node sends the traffic of a service over the mesh to the homelab. There, the homegap-mesh container forwards it to the address of the container of the service. The orchestrator reads that address from Docker. Nothing resolves a name at the time of a connection.

The target is the container that has the labels. To use a different target, set homegap.host to one of these values:

  • An IPv4 address.
  • The name of a container that has a service in its own homegap.* labels. The name of its Compose service also works.

The homegap-mesh container must share a Docker network with the target. HomeGAP selects the address of the target in this order:

  1. The address on a network of a front door container. In the usual stack, this is the Traefik network.
  2. The only address of the target, if the target is on one network.

A target on a different network needs that network on the homegap-mesh service, in compose.override.yml. The file compose.override.example.yml has an example. If HomeGAP finds no address, the log has this warning, and the ports of the service stay closed:

no address for the target <host>: its ports are closed

items.title: When a container is gone
items.text:
When a container with homegap.* labels stops, HomeGAP keeps its services for reconcile.removal_grace (default 3m). After that time, HomeGAP removes the routes and the DNS records of the container.

The grace period prevents a short outage after a restart of the homelab. The orchestrator can start before your app containers. Without the grace period, HomeGAP removes each service and creates it again a moment later.

A new container with the same hostname in its top-level homegap.expose immediately replaces the container that is gone. If the orchestrator cannot list the containers at all, it uses the containers of the last list until Docker answers again.

items.title: Errors and warnings
items.text:
The Services page on the dashboard and the log show the label errors of each container. HomeGAP does not publish a service whose labels have errors. An error about homegap.private_network or homegap.private_hosts that comes from the Docker networks or from the names of the VPN removes only the private path. The public service still publishes. The errors of one container never stop the other services. The errors of a named service start with services.<name>:, and they drop only that service.

A warning does not stop the publication of the service. An unknown homegap.* label gives this warning, and HomeGAP ignores the label:

unknown label '<key>' ignored

items.title: Preview the result of labels
items.text:
The homegap plan command shows what a set of labels produces, without Docker. The input is a JSON file that maps each container name to its labels:

{
  "traefik": {
    "homegap.expose": "example.net",
    "homegap.wildcard": "true",
    "homegap.protocol": "https"
  }
}

The orchestrator process must be able to read the file. If you put the file in the config/ folder next to config.yml and mount it at /config/labels.json, run this command:

docker compose exec orchestrator homegap plan --labels /config/labels.json

The output starts with the ERROR and WARN lines. Then, for each node, it shows the public, private, sni and port items. The dns records come last.

Note

homegap plan does not read Docker networks or the Traefik API. Thus a front door with homegap.private_network or homegap.private_middleware gives errors in the plan output. These errors do not apply to the orchestrator, which reads both.

items.title: Client addresses and private-only services
items.text: This page tells you how to give the homelab the real address of each viewer. It also tells you how to make a Traefik allowlist that only the devices of the VPN pass.

items.title: The problem
items.text:
Every connection reaches the homelab from the homegap-mesh container. Thus the homelab Traefik sees one address for all viewers. HomeGAP has three answers:

  • For a name that a node terminates, the node puts the address of the viewer in the X-Forwarded-For header.
  • homegap.proxy_protocol sends the address of each viewer on a passthrough name and on a raw TCP port.
  • homegap.private_network sends the traffic of VPN devices from a separate network.

items.title: Passthrough names
items.text:
With homegap.proxy_protocol: "true" on the front door, the node adds a PROXY protocol v2 header to the encrypted stream. TLS stays passthrough, and the node reads only the SNI name. The same label works on a dedicated https service in passthrough mode.

The homelab Traefik must trust the header only from the homegap-mesh container. Give homegap-mesh a fixed address on the Traefik network, in compose.override.yml:

services:
  homegap-mesh:
    networks:
      traefik: { ipv4_address: 172.32.0.250 }

Then trust that address on the entrypoint of the homelab Traefik:

entryPoints:
  websecure:
    proxyProtocol:
      trustedIPs: ["172.32.0.250/32"]

Connections without the header continue to work, for example from your LAN and for the health request of each node.

Caution

If you add the label before the entrypoint trusts the header, every TLS handshake through the nodes fails. Configure the entrypoint first.

items.title: Terminated names
items.text: A node that ends TLS for a name sends the request with X-Forwarded-For. To trust it on the homelab Traefik, add forwardedHeaders.trustedIPs to the entrypoint, with the same fixed address.

items.title: Raw ports
items.text: On a raw service, homegap.proxy_protocol: "true" applies to the TCP ports. The agent of the node serves these ports and sends the header. The service must accept PROXY protocol v2. A UDP port has no PROXY protocol, and its service sees the address of the homegap-mesh container. See Raw TCP and UDP.

items.title: Where the label works
items.text: homegap.proxy_protocol is an error on a private service, on a terminated service and on a raw service with UDP ports only.

items.title: Private-only services
items.text:
A private-only service is a name of the front door that only VPN devices can open. The name stays on the homelab Traefik, with its certificate and its routers. This is different from a private service, which has no public path.

With homegap.private_network: "homegap-private", HomeGAP uses a second Docker network that only homegap-mesh and the front door share. Compose adds the project name to the start of the names of project networks. Thus HomeGAP matches a network with exactly the name in the label, or a name that ends in _<label>.

VPN devices resolve each private name to an address of the VPN. The homelab sends the traffic for that address to the front door, with these settings:

  • The destination is the address of the front door on the private network.
  • The ports are homegap.port (443 by default), plus 80 for https.
  • The roles come from homegap.roles. Without the label, only the Admin role gets the private path.
  • The id in the plan is hg-private--<slug of the name>.

The connection leaves homegap-mesh from the private network. Thus the homelab Traefik sees it come from that subnet, and public traffic never has an address in that range. On the private-only routers, accept only that range and your LAN:

http:
  middlewares:
    private-only:
      ipAllowList:
        sourceRange: ["172.33.0.0/24", "192.168.1.0/24"]

Put the middleware on the routers of the private-only services, in labels or in the files of Traefik.

For the users, the roles and the devices of the VPN, see Sign-in and VPN and Users, machines and devices.

items.title: Public traffic never uses the private network
items.text:
The homegap-mesh container is on both networks. To keep public traffic off the private network, HomeGAP sends it to the address of the front door on its other network, unless you set homegap.host.

HomeGAP gives an error in these cases:

Case Result The front door is only on the private network. An error. Public traffic needs another network that the front door shares with homegap-mesh. The front door is on more than one other network. An error. Set homegap.host to the address of the front door on the network that it shares with homegap-mesh. The front door has no address on the named network. An error. HomeGAP removes only the private path. Public traffic does not change.

items.title: Which names get a private path
items.text:
Two labels select the names:

  • homegap.private_hosts gives a list of names.
  • homegap.private_middleware finds the names from the routers of Traefik.

You can use the two labels together or one of them alone. Without both, the private name is the hostname of the service.

HomeGAP adds some names itself, when the front door has a private path:

  • The shared name of the status page.
  • The shared name of the speed test, with speedtest.vpn_access.
  • The name of the dashboard, with dashboard.access: private. See The dashboard for VPN devices only.

items.title: Find the names from the routers
items.text:
With homegap.private_middleware: "private-only@file", HomeGAP reads the routers of this Traefik from its API (/api/http/routers, all pages). It reads only this Traefik. It never reads another Traefik on the host.

Each name in a Host(...) rule of an enabled router that uses the middleware gets a private path. HomeGAP compares the middleware without its @provider part. These rules apply:

  • A name outside the hostname of the front door gets a warning and no private path.
  • HomeGAP cannot read the names of a router with HostRegexp, or of a router without Host. It gives a warning. List those names in homegap.private_hosts.

A service in a subfolder of the root gives the root its private path. An example is a router with Host(`example.net`) && PathPrefix(`/grafana`). VPN devices then reach the whole root over the private network. Its public routers continue to answer them.

items.title: The Traefik API
items.text:
The orchestrator must be able to reach the API of Traefik on the Traefik network. With api.insecure: true in the static config of Traefik, the API answers on port 8080. You do not publish a port for it. To use a different URL, set homegap.traefik_api.

Until the API answers for the first time, HomeGAP does not change the services. The log has the warning cannot read the Traefik API at ..., with the text "services and private paths are left as they are until it answers". homegap plan shows the error the Traefik API at ... has not answered; set homegap.traefik_api if it is elsewhere. After the first answer, a failed read keeps the routers from the last good read.

items.title: Refused names
items.text:
A VPN device must reach some names directly, not through the tunnel. These are the name of the sign-in (sign_in.url), the name in vpn.endpoint and the management host of each node. HomeGAP refuses a private name that covers one of them, with this error:

homegap.private_hosts: '<name>' covers <host>, which VPN devices must reach directly; name the services instead

A device that resolves such a name into the tunnel loses its sign-in on the next reconnect.

Thus HomeGAP refuses *.example.net. A sub-zone such as *.home is correct.

items.title: Example
items.text:
The compose.override.yml of the HomeGAP stack has the fixed address and the private network:

services:
  homegap-mesh:
    networks:
      traefik: { ipv4_address: 172.32.0.250 }
      homegap-private: {}

networks:
  homegap-private:
    ipam: { config: [ { subnet: 172.33.0.0/24 } ] }

The compose file of the homelab Traefik has the labels and joins the network. Compose names the network of the HomeGAP stack homegap_homegap-private:

services:
  traefik:
    labels:
      homegap.expose: "example.net"
      homegap.wildcard: "true"
      homegap.protocol: "https"
      homegap.proxy_protocol: "true"
      homegap.private_network: "homegap-private"
      homegap.private_middleware: "private-only@file"
      homegap.private_hosts: "*.home"
      homegap.roles: "Member"
    networks: [traefik, homegap-private]

networks:
  traefik:
    external: true
  homegap-private:
    name: homegap_homegap-private
    external: true

The homegap.private_hosts label is optional.

items.title: Configure client addresses and private-only services
items.text:
1. Add the homegap-private network to compose.override.yml.
  2. Attach homegap-mesh to this network in the same file.
  3. Give homegap-mesh a fixed address on the Traefik network.
  4. Run docker compose up -d in the folder of the HomeGAP stack. Compose recreates homegap-mesh, and the mesh drops for a moment.
  5. Attach the homelab Traefik to the private network.
  6. Add proxyProtocol.trustedIPs to the entrypoint of Traefik.
  7. If you have terminated services, add forwardedHeaders.trustedIPs with the same address.
  8. Restart Traefik. These settings are in the static config.
  9. Add the labels to the front door.
  10. Add the allowlist middleware to the private-only routers.
  11. Set homegap.roles to the roles that get the private path.
  12. Do the checks in the next section.

items.title: Check the result
items.text:
From the public internet, do these checks:

  • A private-only name returns 403.
  • A public service shows your real IP address in X-Forwarded-For. A whoami service can show this header.

From a device with a Pangolin app, connected to the VPN, do these checks:

  • The private-only name works.
  • The service sees an address in the private subnet.

items.title: On the VPN, a private-only name still returns 403
items.text:
The name has no private path. On the Config page, look at privateNames in the desired state of a node. Also look at the log.

Make sure that the router uses the middleware by its name, on the router itself. HomeGAP reads the middleware list of the router. Or list the name in homegap.private_hosts.

Make sure that the user has a role of homegap.roles on the front door. A device gets a private name only if one of its roles permits it.

items.title: Public traffic comes from the private subnet
items.text: The target of the front door is its private address. Set homegap.host, or keep the front door on only one other network.

items.title: Extra domains
items.text: HomeGAP serves one base domain, the domain of the config file. The management host of each node, the status page, the speed test and the dashboard are always under that domain. This page tells you how to publish services under more domains.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
• Each extra domain needs a DNS zone in the same Bunny account as the zone of domain. HomeGAP uses the same API key for all zones.
  • The registrar of each extra domain must use the Bunny nameservers.
  • An extra domain cannot be inside domain, and domain cannot be inside an extra domain. Two extra domains cannot be inside each other.

items.title: Add an extra domain
items.text:
1. Create the zone of the domain in Bunny DNS.

  2. Add the domain to the config file:

    domain: example.net
bunny:
  zone: example.net

extra_domains:
  - domain: example.org
  - domain: apps.example.io
    zone: example.io

    The zone key is necessary only if the zone is a parent of the domain.

  3. Save the config file. HomeGAP reads it in the next pass.

A new domain does not change the stack of a node. HomeGAP writes the new routes to the routes file of each node, and the Traefik of the node loads them without a restart.

items.title: Check the result
items.text:
1. Open the DNS page of the dashboard.
  2. Find the domain in the Domains table. The State column shows healthy when HomeGAP can sync the zone.
  3. Open the Certificates tab.
  4. Find the CAA records of the domain in Who can issue.

If the State column shows a warning, the usual cause is that the Bunny account has no zone with that name.

items.title: Publish a service under an extra domain
items.text:
Use the same labels as for the base domain. No label names the domain:

labels:
  homegap.expose: shop.example.org
  homegap.port: "8080"

A private service uses the same labels too:

labels:
  homegap.expose: notes.example.org
  homegap.access: private
  homegap.port: "8080"

HomeGAP refuses a hostname that is outside all the domains of the config file. The label error shows the domains that it knows.

items.title: A front door for an extra domain
items.text:
Each domain can have its own front door. The front door of a domain is the public service with the root of that domain in homegap.expose. With homegap.wildcard: "true", it also takes every name one label under the domain that has no service of its own.

Each front door is its own container. In this example, one Traefik is the front door of the base domain. A second Traefik is the front door of an extra domain:

services:
  traefik:
    labels:
      homegap.expose: example.net
      homegap.wildcard: "true"
      homegap.protocol: https
      homegap.tls: passthrough

  other-traefik:
    labels:
      homegap.expose: example.org
      homegap.wildcard: "true"
      homegap.protocol: https
      homegap.tls: passthrough

The front door of an extra domain has these differences from the front door of the base domain:

  • It carries only the names of its own domain.
  • It does not carry the status page or the speed test. Those names stay under the base domain.
  • The health request of Bunny uses the front door of the base domain, if the node serves one.

A domain without a front door serves only the services that name a hostname in it.

items.title: Use only the subdomains of a domain
items.text:
The root of a domain can belong to a service that has no relation to HomeGAP, for example a website at a different host. HomeGAP can still publish services under the subdomains of that domain.

  1. Add the domain to extra_domains, with caa: false: 
    extra_domains:
  - domain: example.org
    caa: false
  2. Do not give the domain a front door. No service has homegap.expose: "example.org".
  3. Publish each service under a subdomain, for example app.example.org. See Publish a service under an extra domain.
  4. Add the records of the root on the Zone records tab of the DNS page, for example an A record for @.

HomeGAP then writes records only for the subdomains that a service uses. It writes no record at the root and no wildcard record, and it does not change the records that you add there.

With caa: false, HomeGAP publishes no CAA records for the domain. Without it, the CAA records of HomeGAP at the root let only Let's Encrypt issue certificates for the domain, and only with the DNS challenge. That stops the certificate of a root service that uses a different authority or a different challenge.

items.title: What HomeGAP does for each extra domain
items.text: Part What HomeGAP does DNS Writes the records of each name to the zone of its domain. Each zone gets the same geo routing and monitors. CAA records Publishes the CAA records at the root of each domain, if acme.caa is on. Certificate Adds each name for which the nodes end TLS to the one certificate of the nodes. A certificate holds 100 names at most. Routes Writes the routes of each name to the routes file of each node that serves it.

items.title: Remove an extra domain
items.text:
1. Remove the labels of each service that uses the domain, or change them to a different domain.
  2. Remove the domain from extra_domains.
  3. Save the config file.

Caution

HomeGAP does not read the zone of a domain that is not in the config file. Records that HomeGAP wrote there stay. Remove the services first, so that HomeGAP deletes their records, and only then remove the domain.

items.title: Label reference
items.text: This page lists every homegap.* label, with its values, its default and its rules. It also tells you how to declare several services on one container.

items.title: Values
items.text:
Label values are text. For a boolean label, use true, 1, yes or on, or false, 0, no or off. The case is not important. Any other value gives the error <key> must be true/false.

For a label with a fixed set of values, any other value gives the error <key> must be one of ... (got '<value>').

items.title: Core labels
items.text: Label Values Default What it does homegap.expose A hostname. None. Each service needs it. Sets the hostname to expose, for example app.example.net, or the root example.net. HomeGAP changes it to lowercase. homegap.wildcard Boolean. false On the root entry, also claims *.<domain>. homegap.protocol http, https, tcp, udp, tcp+udp http, or raw if the port list has protocols. Sets the protocol of the service. For a raw service, it is the default protocol of the ports. homegap.port A port from 1 to 65535. For raw services, a port list. 443 for https, 80 for http. Sets the port of the container. Raw services need it. See Port lists. homegap.tls passthrough, terminate passthrough With passthrough, the node sees only the SNI. With terminate, the node ends TLS. See Traffic paths. homegap.regions Node ids, separated by commas. all Limits the service to these nodes, for example na1,as1. The value all or an empty value selects every node. homegap.access public, private public With private, only the devices of the VPN can reach the service. See Private services. homegap.healthcheck An HTTP path that starts with /, or tcp. None. Sets the path of the health request of Bunny, on the service that this request goes to. See Health resource.

items.title: Rules for the core labels
items.text:
• homegap.expose must be a valid hostname. It must be inside domain or an extra domain, or you get the error "... is outside the managed domain ...".
  • homegap.wildcard is valid only when homegap.expose is the root domain or the root of an extra domain. It is an error on raw services.
  • The node always terminates plain http. If you set homegap.tls: passthrough on an http service, you get the warning plain-http services cannot be passed through; the node terminates TLS (tls=terminate).
  • On raw services, homegap.tls has no effect. HomeGAP gives a warning.
  • An unknown node id in homegap.regions gives the warning "regions reference unknown node(s): ...".
  • If the front door has homegap.tls: terminate and homegap.wildcard, HomeGAP refuses homegap.tls: passthrough on another hostname one label under the domain. See Certificates.
  • Each other value of homegap.healthcheck gives the error homegap.healthcheck must be an HTTP path starting with '/' or 'tcp'. With tcp or without the label, the path of the health request is /.

items.title: Extension labels
items.text:
Label Default What it does homegap.host The container name. Sets the target of the service: an IPv4 address, or a container with a service of its own. See How HomeGAP finds the container. homegap.public_port The value of homegap.port. Sets the public port on the nodes, for a raw service with a single port. homegap.roles None. Lists the roles, separated by commas, whose devices reach a private service or a private path. Without it, only the Admin role reaches the service. homegap.pause false With true, HomeGAP keeps the DNS records of this service as they are. The routes of the service stay. homegap.proxy_protocol false Sends the address of each viewer to the service with PROXY protocol v2. homegap.maintenance_page true on a service that the node terminates. While the homelab is unreachable, the nodes show a "back shortly" page for the service. See When the homelab is down. homegap.private_network None. Names a Docker network that only homegap-mesh and this service share. VPN devices reach the service at its address on that network. homegap.private_hosts The hostname of the service, without homegap.private_middleware. Lists the names, separated by commas, that VPN devices reach through the private network. homegap.private_middleware None. Gives a private path to each name that this Traefik routes through this middleware, for example private-only@file. homegap.traefik_api http://<container name>:8080 Sets the URL of the API of this Traefik, for homegap.private_middleware. The form is http://<host>[:<port>] or https://<host>[:<port>], with no path. The host must be a name without a dot or a private IPv4 address. For other values, HomeGAP gives a warning and uses the default.

These 18 labels are the full set. HomeGAP ignores each other homegap.* label and gives the warning unknown label '<key>' ignored.

items.title: Rules for the extension labels
items.text:
• homegap.public_port on an http or https service gives the warning "... only applies to tcp/udp".
  • With more than one port, or with an entry that has its own public: part, homegap.public_port is an error. Write public:port in homegap.port instead.
  • A hostname that HomeGAP routes itself is an error. These are the management host of each node (node-<id>.<domain>), the names of the status page and the speed test, and the name of the dashboard from dashboard.hostname. The error is hostname N is reserved for HomeGAP.
  • The node uses these ports itself: 80, 443, 8091 and 8092. A public raw service cannot use them as public ports. The error is public port N is reserved on nodes; publish it on another port (public:port in homegap.port, or homegap.public_port). HomeGAP does not check private services, because they publish nothing on the nodes.
  • The UDP port of the mesh (mesh.port, default 51821) gives the error public port N/udp is the port of the mesh.
  • A node also uses its SSH port itself (nodes[].ssh_port, default 22). A public raw service cannot use that port on TCP. The error is public port N/tcp is the SSH port of node <id>. See Use port 22 for a service.
  • The Admin role reaches each private service and each private path. You do not put it in homegap.roles.
  • homegap.proxy_protocol works only on https services in passthrough mode and on raw services with TCP ports, and only on public services. On each other service, it is an error. On a raw service, it applies only to the TCP ports. See Client addresses and private-only services.
  • homegap.maintenance_page needs a service that the node terminates. A passthrough service has no page, because the node holds no certificate for its name. If you set the label to true on a passthrough https service, you get the error "...needs homegap.tls=terminate...". On a raw service, you get the warning "... has no effect on raw ... services".
  • homegap.private_network works only on public http and https services. On each other service, it is an error.
  • homegap.private_hosts and homegap.private_middleware need homegap.private_network.
  • A name in homegap.private_hosts can be relative to the hostname of the service (jellyfin, *.home). It can also be a full name, if that name is the hostname of the service or a name under it. HomeGAP reads each other name as a relative name. You can use * and ?.
  • homegap.private_middleware compares the middleware without its @provider part. HomeGAP reads the routers from the Traefik API.

The nodes use vpn.port and vpn.exit_port (defaults UDP 51830 and 51840) and the port above each for the VPN. A public service cannot take one of these four UDP ports. HomeGAP refuses the service and shows a label error.

items.title: Port lists
items.text:
For a raw service, homegap.port takes a list of entries, separated by commas. Each entry has this form:

[public:]port[/tcp|/udp|/tcp+udp]
Entry Meaning 7881 Port 7881, with the protocol from homegap.protocol. 7881/tcp Port 7881 on TCP. 3478/tcp+udp Port 3478 on TCP and on UDP. HomeGAP also reads udp+tcp as tcp+udp. 2222:22/tcp Public port 2222 on the nodes, to port 22 of the container, on TCP.

These rules apply:

  • A list with a protocol on an entry is a raw service, also without homegap.protocol. For example, homegap.port: "7881/tcp, 7882/udp" is enough.
  • homegap.protocol gives the protocol of the entries without their own protocol. With tcp+udp, each such port is on TCP and UDP. The protocol of an entry has priority.
  • Without homegap.protocol, each entry needs a protocol if one entry has one. Otherwise, you get the error '<entry>' needs a protocol (/tcp, /udp or /tcp+udp), or set homegap.protocol.
  • An http or https service takes only one port number. A list gives the error must be one port number for http services, or for https services.
  • An entry that is not a port from 1 to 65535 gives an error with examples of valid entries.
  • The same public port and protocol twice in one service gives the error is listed twice.

The protocol of the service is the sum of its ports: tcp, udp or tcp+udp. The Services page shows the port list in the Published as column, for example 7881/tcp, 7882/udp. See Raw TCP and UDP.

items.title: Named services
items.text:
One container can declare several services. Put the labels of each service under homegap.services.<name>., for example homegap.services.alt.expose and homegap.services.alt.port. Every label works under this prefix, for example tls, access, healthcheck, proxy_protocol and private_network.

These rules apply:

  • The name has lowercase letters, digits and dashes. It starts and ends with a letter or a digit, and it has 31 characters or fewer (^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,29}[a-z0-9])?$).
  • Each named service needs its own expose. Without it, you get the error services.<name>: homegap.expose is required.
  • The top-level labels of the container are still a service of their own, when the container has homegap.expose.
  • A named service takes these top-level labels as its defaults: homegap.host, homegap.regions, homegap.access, homegap.roles and homegap.pause. It can set its own values.
  • The errors and warnings of a named service start with services.<name>:. An error drops only that service. The other services of the container still publish.
  • An unknown label under a named service gives a warning with the full name of the label.
  • The key of a named service is <host slug>--<name>. HomeGAP uses this key for pause, on the dashboard and in the DNS purpose. The Services page shows the container as <container> · <name>.

items.title: Shared hostnames and ports
items.text:
When two services claim the same thing, the first container in the order of names wins. HomeGAP refuses the later one with an error:

  • Only one http or https service can use a hostname.
  • Raw services can share a hostname with each other, and with one http or https service. DNS has one record set for the hostname, on every node that serves any of these services.
  • Two top-level services on one hostname have the same key. HomeGAP refuses the second one with the error ...already claimed by <container>; give this service a name under homegap.services.. Give the second service a name.
  • On the nodes that two public services share (by homegap.regions), only one service can use a public port and protocol. The error is public port 7882/udp is already used by <container> (<name>). On different nodes, the same port is valid.
  • A raw service on the root domain is never the front door.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
The front door claims the root and the wildcard, with end-to-end TLS:

traefik:
  labels:
    homegap.expose: "example.net"
    homegap.wildcard: "true"
    homegap.protocol: "https"
    homegap.tls: "passthrough"

A private raw TCP service for SSH, for the devices of the role Member:

ssh-jump:
  labels:
    homegap.expose: "ssh.example.net"
    homegap.port: "22"
    homegap.protocol: "tcp"
    homegap.access: "private"
    homegap.roles: "Member"

A public game server on UDP port 27015, in one region:

game:
  labels:
    homegap.expose: "game.example.net"
    homegap.protocol: "udp"
    homegap.port: "27015"
    homegap.regions: "eu1"

A voice server with a port list, and a named service on the same hostname with a different public port:

rtc:
  labels:
    homegap.expose: "rtc.example.net"
    homegap.port: "7881/tcp, 7882/udp, 3478/tcp+udp"
    homegap.services.alt.expose: "rtc.example.net"
    homegap.services.alt.port: "17000:7000/udp"

items.title: Private services
items.text: A private service is available only to the devices of the VPN. This page tells you how HomeGAP publishes a private service, and who can reach it.

items.title: How a private service works
items.text:
With homegap.access: private, a service gets no public DNS record, no public port and no route on a node. HomeGAP gives the service a private name, which only VPN devices resolve and reach:

  • The name is the value of homegap.expose.
  • The destination is the container, or the value of homegap.host.
  • The ports are the ports of the container. For an http or https service, this is homegap.port (default 80 or 443). For a raw service, these are the container ports of the port list, by protocol. A public: part has no effect here.

A device reaches a private service on this path:

  1. A user signs in with a Pangolin app, at the address of sign_in.url. See Connect the Pangolin apps.
  2. The app gets the private names that the roles of the user permit. Each name has an address in vpn.utility_subnet (default 100.96.128.0/24).
  3. The app sends the packets for that address through the tunnel to a node. The node forwards them over the mesh to the homelab.
  4. The homegap-mesh container sends them to the container of the service, on the same port.

HomeGAP ends no TLS for a private service. The device connects directly to the port of the container. The service sees the address of the homegap-mesh container as the source.

Without sign_in.url, there is no sign-in and no VPN, and no device can reach a private service. See Sign-in and VPN.

A private service is different from the private path of a public service. A private service has no public path. For the private path, see Client addresses and private-only services.

items.title: Who can reach a private service
items.text:
The VPN refuses everything by default. A device reaches only the private names that its roles permit, and only on the ports of each service. The firewall of the homegap-mesh container refuses each other packet of a device, also to your home network.

homegap.roles lists the roles that can reach the service, separated by commas:

notes:
  labels:
    homegap.expose: "notes.example.net"
    homegap.access: "private"
    homegap.port: "8080"
    homegap.roles: "Member,family"

These rules apply:

  • The Admin role reaches each private service.
  • A service without homegap.roles is for the Admin role only.
  • A device has the roles of its user. A machine has its own roles.
  • A blocked user, a blocked machine and a blocked device reach nothing.
  • A named service takes homegap.roles and homegap.access from the top-level labels, unless it sets its own values.

You manage the users, the machines and their roles on the Access page of the dashboard. See Users, machines and devices.

items.title: What the service needs at home
items.text:
The homegap-mesh container must share a Docker network with the container of the service. A container on the Traefik network needs no change. For a container on a different network, add that network to the homegap-mesh service in compose.override.yml. See How HomeGAP finds the container.

If HomeGAP finds no address for the service, the log has this warning:

no address for the private target <host>: the VPN does not serve it

items.title: When the homelab is down
items.text: A private service has no path while the homelab is unreachable. A node then signs devices in for the exits only. See Exits and tunnel DNS.

items.title: The dashboard for VPN devices only
items.text:
Warning

If you publish the dashboard to the public, everybody on the internet can reach the control of every node, with only the token as protection. Publish it only to VPN devices.

Do not put homegap.* labels on the orchestrator service for this. Set dashboard.hostname in the config file:

dashboard:
  hostname: orc
  access: private

The Traefik of the homelab then serves the dashboard at orc.<domain>. With dashboard.access: private, which is the default, the name is a private name of the front door. Thus the front door needs homegap.private_network. See Private-only services. The roles come from homegap.roles on the front door.

Without a private path on the front door, the dashboard has no route, and you get this error:

dashboard.access is private, but the front door has no homegap.private_network: the dashboard has no route

For the other keys of dashboard, see the Configuration reference.

items.title: Reach the homelab host over SSH
items.text:
HomeGAP can publish the SSH server of the homelab host as a private service. Then the host accepts SSH from VPN devices, and the internet has no path to it. You set one key in the config file. The compose file needs no change.

  1. Add the key to the config file:

    homelab:
  ssh:
    enabled: true

  2. Save the config file. HomeGAP reads it in the next pass.

  3. On a device, connect the Pangolin app.

  4. Connect to the private name:

    ssh user@ssh.example.net
Key Default What it does homelab.ssh.enabled false Publishes the SSH server of the host as a private service. homelab.ssh.hostname ssh The first label of the private name, <hostname>.<domain>. homelab.ssh.port 22 The port of the SSH server of the host. homelab.ssh.roles [] The roles that can reach the host. The Admin role always can.

For example, to give access to the users with the role Member:

homelab:
  ssh:
    enabled: true
    roles: [Member]

items.title: How HomeGAP finds the host
items.text:
The mesh agent (homegap-mesh-agent) reads the gateway of the default route of its network namespace. This is the address of the Docker host. It writes that address to the file host-gateway in the mesh data folder. The orchestrator uses the address as the destination of the service.

The Services page shows the service with the container name homelab. If the log shows "homelab.ssh waits for the address of the host from the mesh agent", start the homegap-mesh-agent container.

items.title: If the connection fails
items.text:
Look at the host:

  • sshd must listen on an address that a container can reach. The default ListenAddress (all addresses) is correct.
  • The firewall of the host must accept the SSH port from the Docker networks.

items.title: A different service on the host
items.text:
For a service of the host that is not SSH, use labels on a container, with an IPv4 address of the host in homegap.host. The LAN address of the host works. A hostname does not work there, because HomeGAP resolves no name for a target.

Warning

If the front door has a wildcard (homegap.wildcard), public DNS also answers for the private name, with the addresses of the nodes. A device that does not resolve the name through the Pangolin app connects to the SSH server of a node. That server then receives your user name and your password or key. Before you accept a host key, compare its fingerprint with the key of the homelab host.

To read the fingerprint of the host key, run this command on the homelab host:

ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub

items.title: Raw TCP and UDP
items.text: HomeGAP can publish a service that does not use HTTP, for example a game server, a voice server or an SSH jump host. This page tells you how raw TCP and UDP services work.

items.title: The labels
items.text:
A raw service needs these labels:

  • homegap.expose, with a hostname for the service.
  • homegap.port, the port or the list of ports of the container. Raw services need this label.
  • The protocol: homegap.protocol (tcp, udp or tcp+udp), or a protocol on each entry of the port list.

For example, these labels publish TCP 7881 and UDP 7882 without homegap.protocol:

homegap.expose: "voice.example.net"
homegap.port: "7881/tcp, 7882/udp"

For the format of the port list and its rules, see Port lists.

homegap.wildcard is an error on a raw service. homegap.tls has no effect. To limit the nodes that serve the service, use homegap.regions.

items.title: How a raw port works
items.text:
The kernel of the node forwards a raw port. The Traefik of the node has no part in it.

  1. A packet arrives at the public port of the node.
  2. A rule in the chain HG-RAW of the node changes its destination to the same port on the mesh address of the homelab.
  3. The packet goes over the mesh to the homelab.
  4. The homegap-mesh container forwards it to the port of the container of the service.

HomeGAP writes the full set of rules of a node in one step, and the node applies the rules again at boot. The chain HG-RAW-FWD accepts the forwarded connections before the rules of ufw. Thus a new port needs no ufw rule and no restart of a container.

The hostname also gets a geo DNS record set. Raw services that share a hostname share one record set. See Shared hostnames and ports.

The container must have an address that the homegap-mesh container can reach. See How HomeGAP finds the container.

items.title: Public ports
items.text:
The public port of an entry is its public: part. Without it, the public port is the same as the container port. For a service with a single port, homegap.public_port also sets the public port.

HomeGAP refuses public ports that the node uses itself. For the list, see the Label reference.

items.title: Use port 22 for a service
items.text:
A node uses its SSH port itself, so a service cannot have it as a public TCP port. The default SSH port is 22. To give port 22 to a service, for example the SSH of a git server, first move the SSH server of each node that serves the service.

  1. Set ssh_port of each node to a different port, for example 2222. See Node updates and rollback.
  2. Wait until the activity log has the line "moved the SSH server from port 22 to port 2222" for each node.
  3. Add the labels to the service: 
    forgejo:
  labels:
    homegap.expose: "git.example.net"
    homegap.port: "22/tcp"

If a node still has port 22 as its SSH port, HomeGAP refuses the service with the error public port 22/tcp is the SSH port of node <id>. Web traffic for the same hostname does not change. It uses the front door, as before.

Port 22 on the nodes then goes to this service for each hostname, because TCP carries no hostname.

items.title: Ids in the plan
items.text:
The output of homegap plan shows one item for each port and protocol:

Service Id A top-level service with one port and one protocol hg-<host>-<proto>, for example hg-game-example-net-udp. Any other top-level service hg-<host>-<public port>-<proto>, for example hg-voice-example-net-7882-udp. A named service hg-<host>--<name>-<public port>-<proto>, for example hg-rtc-example-net--alt-17000-udp.

items.title: Client addresses
items.text:
A raw service sees the address of the homegap-mesh container as the source of each connection, on TCP and on UDP.

homegap.proxy_protocol: "true" sends the address of each viewer to the service, on the TCP ports only. The service must accept PROXY protocol v2. The kernel cannot add this header, so the agent of the node (homegap-agent) serves these ports:

  1. The agent accepts each connection on the public port.
  2. It opens a connection to the same port on the mesh address of the homelab.
  3. It sends the PROXY protocol header, and then it passes the bytes in both directions.

The agent opens a new port and closes a removed port without a restart. Open connections continue. There is no PROXY protocol for UDP. See Client addresses and private-only services.

items.title: Private raw services
items.text: With homegap.access: private, a raw service gets no public port and no DNS record. Only the devices of the VPN can reach it, on the ports of the container. A public: part has no effect there. See Private services.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
A public game server on UDP port 27015, only on eu1:

game:
  labels:
    homegap.expose: "game.example.net"
    homegap.protocol: "udp"
    homegap.port: "27015"
    homegap.regions: "eu1"

A private SSH jump host on TCP port 22. A private service has no public port, so the SSH port of the nodes does not matter:

ssh-jump:
  labels:
    homegap.expose: "ssh.example.net"
    homegap.port: "22"
    homegap.protocol: "tcp"
    homegap.access: "private"
    homegap.roles: "Member"

A public SSH server on public port 2222, to port 22 of the container:

git-ssh:
  labels:
    homegap.expose: "git.example.net"
    homegap.port: "2222:22/tcp"

A voice server with several ports, and a named service on the same hostname:

rtc:
  labels:
    homegap.expose: "rtc.example.net"
    homegap.port: "7881/tcp, 7882/udp, 3478/tcp+udp"
    homegap.services.alt.expose: "rtc.example.net"
    homegap.services.alt.port: "17000:7000/udp"

For a full example with a chat app and its voice server, see Fluxer.

items.title: Traffic paths
items.text: HomeGAP sends traffic to a service on one of several paths. This page tells you how each path works and when to use it.

items.title: From a node to the homelab
items.text:
Every path uses the mesh between a node and the homelab. Each service has one port on the mesh address of the homelab. The node sends the traffic of the service to that port. There, the homegap-mesh container forwards it to the container of the service. See The mesh.

The orchestrator writes all routes of the Traefik of a node, in one routes file. Traefik loads the file again after each change, without a restart.

The ports of the web services on the mesh address start at node_stack.mesh_port_base (default 40000). Only the nodes can reach them, over the mesh. HomeGAP never publishes these ports.

items.title: Front door, passthrough
items.text:
This is the default path. The homelab Traefik claims the root domain and *.<domain>.

  1. On each node, a Traefik TCP router on :443 reads the TLS SNI. It matches the root and any single label under the domain.
  2. The router forwards the encrypted stream to the port of the front door on the mesh address of the homelab.
  3. The homegap-mesh container forwards the stream to the homelab Traefik.

The node holds no certificate for these names, so it cannot read the traffic. Your certificates stay at home.

The node serves some names itself, so the wildcard passthrough does not include them:

  • The management host of each node, node-<id>.<domain>.
  • The shared names of the status page and the speed test, status.<domain> and speedtest.<domain>. The node sends their requests on to the homelab under its own names, status-<node>.<domain> and speedtest-<node>.<domain>.
  • Dedicated hostnames that use terminate. The name of the sign-in (sign_in.url) is one of them.

On port 80, the node sends a permanent redirect to HTTPS for the passthrough names.

items.title: Front door, terminate
items.text:
With homegap.tls: terminate on the front door, the node ends TLS for the root and the wildcard. It then sends each request over the mesh to the homelab Traefik. The request keeps its host.

The nodes hold a certificate for the root name. With homegap.wildcard, they also hold a certificate for *.<domain>. HomeGAP then refuses passthrough on other hostnames under the domain. See Certificates.

For the hop over the mesh, the node uses the protocol of the service, from homegap.protocol. With https, the node does not check the certificate of the service.

To compare the two modes, change this one label. Use terminate when you need the maintenance page or CrowdSec for the names of the front door.

items.title: Dedicated hostname
items.text:
A labeled service with its own hostname gets its own route on the nodes. This route has priority over the wildcard. A public service also gets its own geo DNS record set.

An https service uses passthrough by default, directly to the service. It has its own SNI route with a higher priority than the front door. The node terminates plain http services, and each https service with homegap.tls: terminate.

HomeGAP orders the certificate of the nodes only for the names that a node terminates.

items.title: Request headers
items.text:
For a name that it terminates, the node adds these headers to each request:

  • X-Forwarded-For, with the address of the viewer.
  • X-HomeGAP-Node, with the id of the node. A viewer cannot set this header.

A passthrough name gets no headers from the node, because the node cannot read the request. For the address of the viewer on a passthrough name, see Client addresses and private-only services.

items.title: Health resource
items.text:
Each node has a health resource, hg-health-<node id>. The Bunny monitor sends its request to the IP address of the node on port 80. The node sends the request over the mesh to the front door. A node can serve no front door of domain. The request then goes to the front door of an extra domain, or to the first dedicated http or https service.

The request has the host header of that service and the path from its homegap.healthcheck (default /). If the node has no route for the request, it answers 502, and Bunny removes the node from the answers.

items.title: When the homelab is down
items.text:
A node shows a "back shortly" page with HTTP status 503 for the names that it terminates:

  • Each service with homegap.tls: terminate, and each plain http service. To disable the page for a service, set homegap.maintenance_page: "false".
  • The shared names of the status page and the speed test.

The homegap-maintenance container of the node checks the homelab over the mesh every 2 seconds. After 3 failed checks in a row, it adds the page. When the homelab answers again, it removes the page.

A passthrough name has no page, because the node holds no certificate for it. The node closes the connection immediately, and the browser shows a connection error. The shared name of the status page tells your users that the homelab is unreachable. Raw ports fail.

items.title: When a browser uses one connection for two names
items.text:
The names on a node have the same IP address. If one certificate is valid for two of them, a browser can use one connection for both names. For example, Firefox opens status.example.net and then sends the requests for app.example.net on the same connection. But the node ends TLS for status.example.net and uses passthrough for app.example.net. Without a correction, the wrong Traefik gets the request and answers 404.

HomeGAP makes each Traefik answer 421 (Misdirected Request) for these requests. The browser then opens a new connection for the name, and the request goes to the correct location.

  • On each node, the route homegap-misdirected matches the names that the node passes through. HomeGAP writes it in the routes file of the node.
  • On the homelab, the route homegap-misdirected matches the names that only the nodes serve. These are the management host of each node, the name of the sign-in, and the shared names of the status page and the speed test. Traefik gets this route from the orchestrator through its HTTP provider. See Install on the homelab. HomeGAP does not include a name that your homelab Traefik routes itself, when it can read the routes of your Traefik. If it cannot read them, it does not include the shared name of the speed test.

Each of these routes uses its own TLS options, homegap-elsewhere. Traefik answers 421 when the TLS options of the route are different from the TLS options of the connection. On a connection for the correct name, no other route matches, and the request goes to its usual route.

A service that ends TLS itself, with no Traefik in front of it, cannot answer 421. If a browser uses the connection of such a service for another name, the service gets the request.

items.title: Comparison
items.text: Passthrough Terminate What the node sees Only the SNI. Plaintext. Where TLS ends On the homelab Traefik, or on the service. On the node. Certificates on the node None for your services. A certificate for each name. See Certificates. Address of the viewer With homegap.proxy_protocol. In X-Forwarded-For. Maintenance page Not possible. Enabled by default. CrowdSec Not possible. Possible, with node_stack.crowdsec.

items.title: Fluxer (chat and voice)
items.text: Fluxer is a self-hosted chat app. Its voice and video calls use a bundled LiveKit server. This page tells you how to publish Fluxer through HomeGAP, with the call media on raw ports.

items.title: How Fluxer uses the network
items.text:
Fluxer uses one domain (FLUXER_DOMAIN). The web app, the API, the gateway and the voice signalling share this domain by path (/api/, /gateway and /livekit). Thus the front door publishes all of them, through your homelab Traefik.

The call media does not use the domain. It goes directly to LiveKit on TCP 7881 and UDP 7882 (FLUXER_LIVEKIT_TCP_PORT and FLUXER_LIVEKIT_UDP_PORT). LiveKit tells the clients a literal address (FLUXER_LIVEKIT_NODE_IP, with FLUXER_LIVEKIT_USE_EXTERNAL_IP=false). The public port must be the same as the container port.

This page gives two setups:

Setup Calls Failover for calls Direct media through one node LiveKit advertises the address of one node. No. TURN (recommended for several nodes) Callers reach a TURN server by name, on the nearest healthy node. Yes.

items.title: The web app
items.text:
1. Put Fluxer in proxy mode. In the .env of Fluxer, set this value: 
    COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:docker-compose.proxy.yml
    In proxy mode, the edge of Fluxer listens on plain HTTP port 8080 for your proxy. FLUXER_EDGE_BIND sets the address on the host.
  2. Attach the edge service of Fluxer to the Traefik network, in a compose override of Fluxer: 
    services:
  edge:
    networks: [fluxer, traefik]

networks:
  traefik:
    external: true
  3. Route chat.example.net from your homelab Traefik to the edge, for example in the dynamic config: 
    http:
  routers:
    fluxer:
      rule: "Host(`chat.example.net`)"
      entryPoints: [websecure]
      service: fluxer
      tls: {}
  services:
    fluxer:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: "http://fluxer-edge-1:8080"
    Replace fluxer-edge-1 with the name of the edge container.

The front door publishes chat.example.net. The web app needs no HomeGAP labels.

The proxy requirements of Fluxer apply to your Traefik as usual: WebSocket upgrades, long timeouts and bodies up to 512 MB. See the reverse proxy guide of Fluxer.

items.title: The network of LiveKit
items.text:
The homelab forwards the raw ports from the homegap-mesh container. Thus homegap-mesh must join the Docker network of Fluxer. With the project name fluxer, this network is fluxer_fluxer. Add it to the homegap-mesh service in the compose.override.yml of the HomeGAP stack:

services:
  homegap-mesh:
    networks:
      fluxer: {}

networks:
  fluxer:
    external: true
    name: fluxer_fluxer

Then run this command in the folder of the HomeGAP stack:

docker compose up -d

Caution

Compose recreates the homegap-mesh container after this change. The mesh drops, and the nodes cannot reach the homelab until the container runs again.

Caution

Keep LiveKit (and coturn) on one Docker network only: the network that it shares with homegap-mesh. HomeGAP uses the only address of a container that is not on the Traefik network. With two such networks, HomeGAP finds no address, and the ports stay closed. Thus join homegap-mesh to the network of Fluxer. Do not add a network to LiveKit.

items.title: Setup 1: direct media through one node
items.text:
In this setup, all calls go through one node. It is the simpler setup, but calls have no failover.

  1. In a compose override of Fluxer, remove the published ports of the livekit service, and add the labels: 
    services:
  livekit:
    ports: !reset []
    labels:
      homegap.expose: "voice.example.net"
      homegap.port: "7881/tcp, 7882/udp"
      homegap.regions: "na1"
  2. In the .env of Fluxer, set the public IPv4 address of that node: 
    FLUXER_LIVEKIT_NODE_IP=203.0.113.10
FLUXER_LIVEKIT_USE_EXTERNAL_IP=false
  3. Restart Fluxer.

We recommend homegap.regions with the advertised node, so that HomeGAP publishes the ports only there. With all nodes, calls still use only the advertised node.

The kernel of the node forwards the two ports over the mesh to LiveKit. LiveKit sees each caller at the address of the homegap-mesh container.

items.title: Setup 2: TURN
items.text:
In this setup, calls reach a TURN server by name. DNS sends each caller to the nearest healthy node, so failover also works for calls. We recommend it when you have several nodes.

  1. Add coturn on the network of Fluxer, in a compose override of Fluxer: 
    services:
  turn:
    image: docker.io/coturn/coturn:4.7.0
    command:
      - --listening-port=3478
      - --realm=example.net
      - --use-auth-secret
      - --static-auth-secret=<secret>
      - --min-port=49160
      - --max-port=49200
      - --allowed-peer-ip=<the Docker network range of LiveKit>
      - --no-tls
      - --no-dtls
      - --no-cli
      - --fingerprint
    networks: [fluxer]
    labels:
      homegap.expose: "turn.example.net"
      homegap.port: "3478/tcp+udp"
  2. In the .env of Fluxer, set the TURN servers. Use the same secret as coturn: 
    FLUXER_LIVEKIT_TURN_SERVERS='[{"host":"turn.example.net","port":3478,"protocol":"udp","secret":"<secret>"},{"host":"turn.example.net","port":3478,"protocol":"tcp","secret":"<secret>"}]'
  3. In the same file, leave the node address empty: 
    FLUXER_LIVEKIT_NODE_IP=
FLUXER_LIVEKIT_USE_EXTERNAL_IP=false
  4. Make sure that the livekit service has no HomeGAP labels and no published ports.
  5. Restart Fluxer.

LiveKit then advertises its container address, and only coturn can reach it. With a secret, coturn checks short-lived credentials (use-auth-secret). The host of a TURN server can be a hostname.

Every node forwards port 3478 on TCP and UDP to coturn. The relay ports of coturn (49160 to 49200) stay on the Docker network of Fluxer. They need no labels.
